winner.name: verifiability
winner.summary: TransparentSortPass runs as four kernels in two WGSL modules. A deterministic GATHER compacts cull regions 14..25 in region-major order into (key, slot) pairs in buffer A. From the same kernel it also writes the draw args and a sort-state header: n = min(raw, limit), overflow flag, tile count. A classic reduce-then-scan LSD radix sort follows: 7 passes of 8-bit digits over the 52-bit key (zKey<<20 | id). Each pass is 3 dispatches: UPSWEEP (per-tile 256-bin histogram in workgroup atomics), SCAN (a single workgroup does a column-wise exclusive scan over tiles, then a 256-entry scan of the digit totals; the dispatch boundary is the only global barrier, so no workgroup waits on another), and SCATTER (stable in-tile ranking without subgroups). The ranking handles a tile of 1024 as 4 ordered rounds of 256. Within a round each element's rank is the popcount of lower-thread bits in a per-digit 256-bit mask in workgroup memory, and a per-digit cursor carries the offset from one round to the next. So each element lands exactly at its textbook stable counting-sort position. All keys are unique because ids are unique, so the correct output is one exact permutation: it is identical every frame and can be compared bit for bit with a JS sort. Per-pass parameters are constant 256-byte uniform slices written once at setup, one bind group per pass. The only per-frame writes are one 16-byte GatherParams and the state/diag reset, both in prepare(). Every buffer is fixed-size at MAX_ENTITIES, so capacity overflow cannot happen by construction. The only reachable over-count is a wrong CPU bound: it is clamped, flagged in the state header, and checked every frame in dev. A CPU model runs each kernel in barrier phases with shuffled thread and workgroup order and a workgroup-memory race checker. It mirrors every GPU buffer word for word, and a dev per-stage readback compares each kernel's GPU output with it. Estimated cost at 100k: about 0.35-0.8 ms on the iGPU.

kernels.name: gather (ts/src/shaders/transparent-gather.wgsl, entry gather_main)
kernels.dispatch: ceil(L / 256) workgroups, 1-D, computed on the CPU from L = min(transparentCount, MAX_ENTITIES=100000); 391 at L=100k. Not dispatched at all when L == 0.
bindings: b0 uniform GatherParams { limit: u32, regionSize: u32, _pad0: u32, _pad1: u32 } (16 B, own buffer, minBindingSize 16) - read
b1 var<storage, read> drawArgs: array<u32>  <- 'indirect-args' (28x5 u32) - read
b2 var<storage, read> visibleIndices: array<u32>  <- 'visible-indices' - read
b3 var<storage, read> bounds: array<vec4<u32>>  <- 'entity-bounds' read as BIT PATTERNS (.z), so no float op touches z - read
b4 var<storage, read> entityIds: array<u32>  <- 'entity-ids' (new) - read
b5 var<storage, read_write> keysOut: array<vec2<u32>>  <- 'sort-keys-a' - write
b6 var<storage, read_write> valsOut: array<u32>  <- 'sort-vals-a' - write
b7 var<storage, read_write> state: SortState  <- 'transparent-args' (64 B: DrawIndexedIndirect 5 u32, then rawCount, limit, overflow, numTiles, 7 reserved; minBindingSize 64) - write
kernels.algorithm: 1) lid==0 serially reads the 12 counts drawArgs[(14+k)*5+1], k=0..11 (regions 14..25 = prim types 0..5 x 2 buckets; Light2D slots 26/27 and the opaque buckets are never read) and stores the inclusive prefix in regionEnd[12] (workgroup memory, 48 B). 2) workgroupBarrier(): top level, the kernel's only barrier. 3) raw = regionEnd[11]; n = min(raw, limit). 4) wid==0 && lid==0 writes state = {indexCount 6, instanceCount n, firstIndex 0, baseVertex 0, firstInstance 0, rawCount raw, limit, overflow u32(raw > limit), numTiles ceil(n/1024)}. firstInstance 0 means the draw needs no indirect-first-instance, and a single writer means no atomics. 5) i = wid*256 + lid; if (i >= n) return (after the barrier, so uniformity is not an issue). 6) k = number of q in 0..11 with regionEnd[q] <= i; start = k ? regionEnd[k-1] : 0; j = i - start; slot = visibleIndices[(14+k)*regionSize + j]. 7) zb = bounds[slot].z; if zb == 0x80000000 then zb = 0 (-0 becomes +0, an integer compare so denormal flushing cannot interfere); zKey = (zb & 0x80000000) ? ~zb : zb | 0x80000000; id = entityIds[slot] & 0xFFFFF. 8) keysOut[i] = vec2u((zKey << 20) | id, zKey >> 12); valsOut[i] = slot. Determinism: output i is a pure function of the 12 counts and the region contents. Only the order inside a region varies between frames, never the multiset, and the sort erases that order because every key is unique.

kernels.name: upsweep (ts/src/shaders/transparent-sort.wgsl, entry upsweep_main)
kernels.dispatch: ceil(L / 1024) workgroups (98 at 100k), one per tile, CPU-computed. Tiles with t*1024 >= n return at once. 7 dispatches per frame, one per radix pass, each with bind group p.
bindings: Shared sort layout (one explicit layout for upsweep/scan/scatter, 1 uniform + 6 storage):
b0 uniform PassParams { passIndex: u32, _pad0: u32, _pad1: u32, _pad2: u32 } - slice at offset 256*p of 'sort-pass-params', size 16 - read
b1 var<storage, read> keysIn: array<vec2<u32>> (A if p even, else B) - read
b2 var<storage, read> valsIn: array<u32> - declared in layout, unused here
b3 var<storage, read_write> keysOut: array<vec2<u32>> - declared in layout, unused here
b4 var<storage, read_write> valsOut: array<u32> - declared in layout, unused here
b5 var<storage, read> state: SortState <- 'transparent-args' (read-only view, so state.instanceCount is a UNIFORM value) - read
b6 var<storage, read_write> hist: SortHist { diag: array<atomic<u32>,16>, digitBase: array<u32, 7*256>, tiles: array<u32> } <- 'sort-hist' - write tiles
kernels.algorithm: n = state.instanceCount; t = wid.x; if (t*1024 >= n) return. This is uniform control flow: wid is a uniform builtin, and a load from var<storage, read> is uniform under WGSL uniformity analysis. Phase 0: atomicStore(&wgHist[lid], 0); workgroupBarrier(). Phase 1: load the 4 keys first (i_r = t*1024 + r*256 + lid, r=0..3, only if i_r < n), then atomicAdd(&wgHist[digit(key_r, p)], 1). digit(k,p) = ((p < 4 ? k.x : k.y) >> ((p & 3)*8)) & 0xFF; pass 6 only ever sees digits 0..15. workgroupBarrier(). Phase 2: hist.tiles[t*256 + lid] = atomicLoad(&wgHist[lid]). The counts do not depend on atomic order, so the result is deterministic. Only rows t < numTiles(n) are written, and only those are read later.

kernels.name: scan (transparent-sort.wgsl, entry scan_main)
kernels.dispatch: 1 workgroup per radix pass (7 per frame), with bind group p. Its dispatch boundary is the global barrier between upsweep and scatter, so it relies on no cross-workgroup forward progress.
bindings: same shared layout as upsweep; uses b0 PassParams (read), b5 state (read), b6 hist (read_write: tiles in place, digitBase[p], diag)
kernels.algorithm: Thread d owns digit d. n = state.instanceCount; T = ceil(n/1024). There is no early return, and n=0 works naturally. 1) Column scan: sum = 0; for t in 0..T-1: c = tiles[t*256+d]; tiles[t*256+d] = sum; sum += c. Addresses are coalesced across threads for each t. The loop is written as chunks of 8 guarded loads, then the adds, so 98 tiles cost about 13 L2 round trips instead of 98. 2) totals[d] = sum; workgroupBarrier(). 3) Hillis-Steele inclusive scan over totals[256]: for off = 1,2,..,128 (constant loop, so uniform): v = d >= off ? totals[d-off] : 0; workgroupBarrier(); totals[d] += v; workgroupBarrier(). 4) incl = totals[d]; hist.digitBase[p*256 + d] = incl - sum (exclusive). digitBase is kept PER PASS, so a readback can check all 7 global histograms. 5) GPU self-check: if d == 255 && incl != n, atomicOr(&hist.diag[0], 1). All arithmetic is integer, so the result does not depend on the scan algorithm.

kernels.name: scatter (transparent-sort.wgsl, entry scatter_main)
kernels.dispatch: ceil(L / 1024) workgroups (98 at 100k), one per tile, CPU-computed; tiles with t*1024 >= n return. 7 dispatches per frame with bind group p (p even: A to B, p odd: B to A; pass 6 ends in B = 'transparent-order').
bindings: same shared layout; b0 PassParams read; b1 keysIn read; b2 valsIn read; b3 keysOut write; b4 valsOut write; b5 state read; b6 hist read_write (tiles and digitBase read, diag atomicOr)
kernels.algorithm: Workgroup memory: masks: array<atomic<u32>, 2048> (256 digits x 8 words = one bit per thread, 8192 B) and cursor: array<u32, 256> (1024 B). n = state.instanceCount; t = wid.x; if (t*1024 >= n) return (uniform, as in upsweep). Tile element order is ROUND-MAJOR: element (r, j) = input index t*1024 + r*256 + j, which is the input order. PHASE 0: preload the 4 (key, val) pairs per thread into private registers (active_r = i_r < n); cursor[j] = hist.digitBase[p*256+j] + hist.tiles[t*256+j]; thread j clears masks[j*8 .. j*8+7] (atomicStore 0). workgroupBarrier() [B0]. Then for r in 0..3 (constant loop, so every barrier is in uniform control flow; inactive threads do nothing but still hit every barrier): (a) if active: d = digit(key_r,p); atomicOr(&masks[d*8 + j/32], 1u << (j%32)); workgroupBarrier() [B1]. (b) if active: total = sum over w=0..7 of countOneBits(masks[d*8+w]); rank = popcount of words w < j/32 + countOneBits(masks[d*8+j/32] & ((1u << (j%32)) - 1u)); base = cursor[d]. No writes in this phase. workgroupBarrier() [B2]. (c) if active: dst = base + rank; if (dst < n) { keysOut[dst] = key_r; valsOut[dst] = val_r } else atomicOr(&hist.diag[0], 2); atomicStore(&masks[d*8 + j/32], 0), where several threads may store 0 to the same word atomically; if (rank == total-1) cursor[d] = base + total, exactly one writer per digit and no reader in this phase. workgroupBarrier() [B3], which keeps the clear away from the next round's atomicOr. That is 13 barriers per tile. STABILITY PROOF: dst = (#elements with digit < d, from digitBase) + (#digit-d elements in earlier tiles, from the column scan) + (#digit-d elements in earlier rounds of this tile, from cursor) + (#digit-d elements at lower thread index in this round, from the mask popcount). That equals the number of elements ordered before this one by (digit, input index), which is exactly the stable counting-sort position. With 7 stable passes, LSD sorts by the full 52-bit key. No atomic's order ever reaches an address; masks are OR-ed and popcounted, which is commutative.

buffers: entity-ids (renderer, pool): MAX_ENTITIES x 4 B = 400,000 B; STORAGE | COPY_DST (+COPY_SRC dev). array<u32> slot -> external id, uploaded whole only on frames where the slot->id mapping changed (decided elsewhere); read by gather b4.

transparent-args (renderer, pool): 16 u32 = 64 B; STORAGE | INDIRECT | COPY_DST (+COPY_SRC dev). Words 0-4 DrawIndexedIndirect {6, n, 0, 0, 0} for ForwardPass's single uber draw (offset 0); 5 rawCount, 6 limit, 7 overflow, 8 numTiles, 9-15 reserved. Reset by writeBuffer in prepare() each frame, written on the GPU by gather wg0/lid0, read-only in the sort kernels (source of n).

transparent-order (renderer, pool) = vals B: MAX_ENTITIES x 4 = 400,000 B; STORAGE (+COPY_SRC dev). The sorted entity slots, ascending (zKey, id) = back to front. Bound as group-0 binding 2 of the uber pipeline and read as order[instance_index] (firstInstance 0). Written by scatter on even passes (0,2,4,6).
sort-keys-a (renderer, pool, internal): MAX_ENTITIES x 8 = 800,000 B; STORAGE (+COPY_SRC dev). array<vec2<u32>> (lo = zKey<<20 | id, hi = zKey>>12). Gather output; ping side A.
sort-vals-a (renderer, pool, internal): MAX_ENTITIES x 4 = 400,000 B; STORAGE (+COPY_SRC dev). Slots, ping side A.
sort-keys-b (renderer, pool, internal): 800,000 B; STORAGE (+COPY_SRC dev). Pong side B keys; after pass 6 it holds the sorted keys (kept for the dev readback check).

sort-hist (renderer, pool, internal): (16 + 7*256 + ceil(100000/1024)*256) u32 = (16 + 1792 + 25088) x 4 = 107,584 B; STORAGE | COPY_DST (+COPY_SRC dev). struct SortHist { diag: array<atomic<u32>,16>, digitBase: array<u32,1792>, tiles: array<u32> }. diag[0] bit0 = scan sum != n, bit1 = scatter dst >= n. diag is zeroed by writeBuffer in prepare(). digitBase is kept per pass; the tile table is reused by every pass. minBindingSize 7236.

sort-gather-params (pass-owned uniform): 16 B, UNIFORM | COPY_DST; GatherParams {limit, regionSize (=100000, exported from cull-pass.ts as VISIBLE_REGION_SIZE), _pad0, _pad1}; written ONCE per frame in prepare().
sort-pass-params (pass-owned uniform): 7 x 256 = 1792 B, UNIFORM | COPY_DST; slice p holds PassParams {passIndex=p, 0, 0, 0}; written ONCE at setup (constants), never per frame.

dev only: a 3-deep MAP_READ ring of 128 B (transparent-args 64 B + sort-hist diag 64 B), copied after the pass every frame; plus on-demand staging buffers for engine.debug.readTransparentSort() (inputs: indirect-args, the first L entries of visible-indices regions 14..25, entity-bounds, entity-ids; outputs: keys/vals A after gather and after each pass when {stages:true}, final keys-b/order, sort-hist, transparent-args).

Total device memory (production): ~2.91 MB, fixed at MAX_ENTITIES. Grow-only reallocation and bind-group rebuilds are not needed; 22 bind groups (1 gather + 7 sort, each pass's bind group serving upsweep, scan and scatter) are created once in setup().
winner.uniformHandling: Two uniform buffers, neither ever rewritten between passes of a frame. (1) PassParams: the per-radix-pass data is the constant passIndex, and the shader derives word = p<4 ? lo : hi and shift = (p&3)*8. It lives in 7 slices of 256 B (minUniformBufferOffsetAlignment) in 'sort-pass-params', written by a single writeBuffer at setup(). One bind group per pass p points at offset 256*p, size 16, and also bakes in the ping-pong direction (p even: A to B, p odd: B to A), so execute() only selects bind group p and issues no writeBuffer at all. (2) GatherParams {limit, regionSize, _pad0, _pad1} is the only per-frame value, written once in prepare(). Both structs are 4 x u32 with explicit trailing pads, so they have no implicit padding and uniform-layout.test.ts covers them automatically, since it globs every *.wgsl. Both layout entries set minBindingSize 16. The dynamic count n is deliberately NOT a uniform: it only exists on the GPU. The sort kernels read it from 'transparent-args' bound as var<storage, read>, a read-only module-scope variable whose loads are uniform, so the tile guard `if (t*1024 >= n) return` can precede the barriers. prepare() also writes the state reset (64 B) and the diag zeroing (64 B), once per frame each. They land before the submit and the GPU overwrites the state in the same frame. No pipeline overrides are needed; only compile-time consts (TILE, ROUNDS, RADIX, PASSES, FIRST_BUCKET=14, GATHER_BUCKETS=12) are used, and a text-agreement test pins them against the TS constants.
winner.countHandling: CPU side: L = min(transparentCount, MAX_ENTITIES). transparentCount comes from Rust and counts every Transparent entity, including transparent Light2D and culled ones, so it is an upper bound. L == 0: prepare() writes transparent-args = {6,0,0,0,0,...}, execute() encodes nothing, profileStages() returns [], and ForwardPass skips the uber draw on the same CPU condition; the args are valid (zero instances) regardless. L > 0: gather gets ceil(L/256) workgroups, upsweep/scatter get ceil(L/1024) each, scan gets 1, so the dispatch capacity ceil(L/1024)*1024 is >= L >= n always. GPU side: raw = sum of instanceCount over buckets 14..25 (lights 26/27 excluded); n = min(raw, L); overflow = raw > L; numTiles = ceil(n/1024). All of it is written to transparent-args by gather, and the draw's instanceCount IS n. Capacity cannot be exceeded by construction: every buffer holds MAX_ENTITIES, and cull cannot emit more than entityCount <= MAX_ENTITIES (the SoA uploads already fail beyond that). The only reachable over-count is a wrong CPU bound, for example a Mode A bridge not carrying transparentCount, or a meta/ECS mismatch. That case is clamped (the draw shows the first L gathered entries in region-major order, dropping the tail of the last regions, a nondeterministic subset) and flagged. Dev builds read state and diag back every frame through a 3-deep MAP_READ ring and warn once when overflow != 0 or diag != 0 or instanceCount != min(raw, limit). Empty after culling (n = 0 with L > 0): every upsweep/scatter workgroup returns at its uniform guard, scan runs with T = 0 and checks incl(255) == 0 == n, and the draw has 0 instances. n = 1: one tile, one active thread per round-0; each pass puts it at dst 0. Non-multiple of the tile: in the last tile, threads with i >= n are inactive in every phase (no histogram count, no mask bit, no write) but execute every barrier. Workgroups beyond numTiles exit before any barrier. The scatter's dst < n guard means a bug can never write out of range; it sets diag bit 1 instead.
winner.bandwidthEstimate100k: N = 100,000; per-element traffic. GATHER: reads visible-indices 4 B + entity-bounds 16 B (a vec4 line share; slots within a cull region arrive roughly ascending) + entity-ids 4 B, writes keys 8 B + vals 4 B = 36 B, so 3.6 MB. Pessimistic, with fully random slots costing a 64 B line each for bounds and ids: 4+64+64+12 = 144 B, so 14.4 MB. PER RADIX PASS: upsweep reads keys 8 B (only one word is used, but the vec2 line comes along); scatter reads keys 8 + vals 4 and writes keys 8 + vals 4. That is 32 B x 1e5 = 3.2 MB, plus the tile table (98 x 256 x 4 = 100 KB) written by upsweep, read+written by scan and read by scatter, about 0.4 MB, for 3.6 MB per pass. x 7 passes = 25.2 MB. TOTAL: about 28.8 MB typical, 39.6 MB pessimistic. At 60 GB/s: 0.48 ms (0.66 ms pessimistic); at 100 GB/s: 0.29 ms (0.40 ms). Fixed costs: 22 dependent dispatches x ~2-5 us of pipeline drain = 0.04-0.11 ms. The single-workgroup scan chain (13 chunks of L2 loads) is about 5 us x 7 = 0.035 ms. Scatter compute (13 barriers + 8 LDS loads + popcounts per round, 98 workgroups on 12 CUs, about 1-2 waves of residency at 9 KB LDS each) is about 5-8 us per pass, largely overlapped with its memory traffic. Estimate: about 0.35-0.8 ms < 1 ms. It is pessimistic in one respect: each pass's working set (1.2 MB in + 1.2 MB out + 0.1 MB table) mostly stays in the iGPU's L2, and upsweep then scatter re-read the same keys, so the real DRAM traffic is lower. Scattered writes form per-digit runs (in-tile runs are adjacent to the neighbouring tiles' runs of the same digit), which combine in L2. The number must be confirmed with the staged profiler (transparent-sort/gather|upsweep|scan|scatter) on the AMD iGPU at 100k. If scatter dominates, the first optimisation is to fuse upsweep p+1 into scatter p through global atomicAdd on tiles[dst/1024][digit_{p+1}] (commutative, so still deterministic). That saves 0.8 MB and one dispatch per pass.
winner.cpuReference: ts/src/render/passes/transparent-sort-reference.ts, with the constants in transparent-sort-constants.ts shared with the pass. It is a phase-level simulator of the SAME kernels, not a different sort. (1) Buffers are Uint32Arrays with the exact GPU word layouts: state 16 words, SortHist 16+1792+98*256, keys as interleaved lo/hi, vals. A GPU readback can therefore be compared word for word. (2) Each kernel (cpuGather, cpuUpsweep, cpuScan, cpuScatter) is a list of phases, one per barrier interval, mirroring the WGSL line by line. A driver runs the workgroups of a dispatch in a caller-chosen order (shuffled in tests: this models no inter-workgroup ordering). Inside a workgroup, phase k runs for all 256 threads in a caller-chosen permutation before phase k+1 starts, which models the barrier. (3) Workgroup memory goes through a SharedMemory wrapper that logs each thread's non-atomic reads and writes per phase and throws when another thread touches a written address in the same phase. This race checker proves the barrier placement (for example cursor written only in B2-B3, read only in B1-B2, masks only through atomics). Atomics are modelled as commutative ops (OR, add, store 0). (4) Keys use sortableZBits(bits) exactly as in WGSL (-0 normalization by integer compare, then the sign flip), tested against the existing floatToSortKey for all non-negative-zero inputs. Headless tests: the full pipeline equals an oracle (Array.sort by (zKey, id)) on random inputs of size 0, 1, 2, 255, 256, 257, 1023, 1024, 1025, 2047, 4097 and 100000, over distributions such as all-equal z (ties resolved by ascending id), 2 z values, all-distinct, descending, ids 0 and 0xFFFFF, and z = +/-0, denormals, +/-Inf. Each scatter pass equals a textbook stable counting sort on its digit. digitBase[p] equals the exclusive scan of the global digit-p histogram of the final keys, which is order-independent and so also assertable on a GPU readback. The output is invariant under shuffled region contents (cull nondeterminism), shuffled tile order and shuffled thread order. Overflow (raw > L): n = L, flag set, args {6,L,0,0,0}. Empty input: args {6,0,0,0,0} and no writes. Buckets 26/27 and 0..13 are never read. Text-agreement tests pin the WGSL consts, entry points, binding types vs layouts, storage count per layout (gather 7, sort 6, both <= 8, every declared binding read), workgroup bytes per entry point (48/1024/1024/9216 <= 16384) and PASSES odd (result in B = transparent-order). Pass tests on a mock device check: pass-params written exactly once at setup, gather-params once per prepare, no writeBuffer in execute, 22 compute passes, bind group p at offset 256p with the right A/B direction, dispatch sizes 391/98/1 at L=100k, profileStages length == mark calls. GPU side (dev, Mode B/C): engine.debug.readTransparentSort({stages:true}) copies the frame's gather inputs and every stage's A/B buffers in the same command buffer. The CPU model, fed with those exact inputs, must reproduce every stage bit for bit, which pinpoints the first kernel that diverges. The final order must also equal the oracle, be strictly increasing and a permutation of the gathered slots, with diag == 0, and be identical across two consecutive frames. The dev ring checks state/diag on every frame. A probe pixel check in the 2D Twins tab (quad under box shadow, different types, depth order) and profiler timing at 100k close it.
risks: Uniformity: the tile guard `if (t*1024 >= n) return` before barriers relies on loads from var<storage, read> being uniform (read-only module-scope variable). The spec and Tint say so; if a compiler rejects it, fall back to lid0 -> workgroup var -> workgroupUniformLoad. Validate with getCompilationInfo and error-scoped pipeline creation on the AMD adapter before anything else.

Fixed cost for small scenes: 22 dependent dispatches (about 0.05-0.1 ms of drain/barrier) are paid even for 2 transparent sprites. Mitigations, after measuring only: a single-workgroup small-n kernel, or indirect dispatch to skip passes whose digit is constant (visible in the digitBase readback).

Scatter writes directly to global memory (no shared-memory local sort, which does not fit in 16 KB next to the 8 KB masks at TILE 1024). If scatter dominates the profile, the options are the fused upsweep (global atomics, still deterministic) or TILE 512 with a local sort.
Single-workgroup scan latency (98 sequential tile rows per pass). It is chunked by 8 loads, but it depends on the compiler unrolling the constant inner loop; measure the transparent-sort/scan stage.

transparentCount must be a true upper bound in every mode. Mode A's bridge and render worker must carry it and entity-ids, which is outside this pass. A wrong bound means silently dropped entities in production; only the dev ring catches it.
A stale entity-ids buffer (mapping changed but not re-uploaded) gives a wrong tie-break without any GPU diag. Only the readback's key == makeKey(bounds, ids) check sees it.

The CPU model and the WGSL are two codebases: correspondence is by line-by-line mirroring, constant/layout text tests and the per-stage GPU readback, not by construction. The race checker validates the model's barrier placement, not the WGSL's.
Ping-pong parity: PASSES = 7 (odd) puts the result in B = transparent-order. Changing DIGIT_BITS flips it; a test pins the parity and the resource name.
LDS atomic contention when digits concentrate (all z equal, pass 6 with 16 digits): up to 32-way conflicts on one mask word. Correct, but slower; the worst case must be profiled too.

Dev-only COPY_SRC usage on the sort buffers and the per-frame 128 B ring mean dev and production differ in usage flags and in one tiny copy; timing must be read on a build without an active full readback.
The new shaders need shaderSlots entries (throwaway probe pass, usedBy) for hot reload; otherwise a broken edit is only caught at graph rebuild.

Profiler: 22 extra markers per measured frame (the budget is 256, shared with LightGroupsPass stages). A mark-count mismatch drops the frame silently, so the test comparing profileStages with mark calls is required.

scores.name: verifiability
scores.notes: The reduce-then-scan structure is sound. Budgets check out: gather has 7 storage + 1 uniform, the sort layout 6 + 1 (all within 8). Workgroup memory is 48, 1024, 1024 and 9216 B, all within 16384. The scatter ranking is stable. Round-major order (i = t*1024 + r*256 + j) plus a popcount of the lower lanes' bits plus a cursor gives the textbook stable counting-sort position. The clear is correct: each active thread atomicStores 0 to its own mask word, so every non-zero word is cleared. Exactly one writer (rank == total-1) advances the cursor in phase c, and no thread reads it in that phase. B1, B2 and B3 separate every write/read pair. The global scan is a separate single-workgroup dispatch, so there is no cross-workgroup forward progress. The column walk is chunked by 8 to hide L2 latency. Per-pass params are constant 256-B slices written once at setup; only GatherParams and the args/diag resets are written per frame, in prepare(). The early exit `if (t*1024 >= n) return` before the barriers depends on loads from var<storage, read> being uniform. I believe the WGSL spec says they are, and the design names a workgroupUniformLoad fallback. Validate that on the AMD adapter first. The heavy work follows the visible count n: tiles past n exit. The draw args are reset every frame, so a skipped frame never replays stale slots. Verification is the strongest of the three: a phase-level CPU simulator with shuffled workgroup and thread order, a workgroup-memory race checker, per-pass digitBase that can be checked on a readback, GPU diag bits (scan sum != n, dst >= n), and a per-stage GPU readback compared bit for bit. Weaknesses: the upsweep reads 8 B keys when it needs one word. With all z equal, a pass-3..6 upsweep sends all 1024 elements of a tile to one LDS bin, a 1024-way serialized atomicAdd. It writes the keys again in pass 6 only for the readback. The text claims '22 bind groups' but the design has 1 + 7 = 8. The dev MAP_READ ring every frame and the per-stage staging add infrastructure. Estimate: 0.35-0.8 ms at 100k over 22 dispatches, plausible within 1 ms.

scores.name: simplicity
scores.notes: This is the cleanest of the three: 4 pipelines, 2 layouts (7+1 and 5+1 storage/uniform entries), and 9216 B of workgroup memory in scatter. The scatter ranking uses the same round-major popcount-plus-cursor scheme. It is stable, and B0-B3 separate the reads from the writes. The scan is a single-workgroup dispatch, so there is no forward-progress assumption. Padding to whole tiles with max-key sentinels removes every bounds check. I checked the sentinel: its id byte 2 is 0xFF against at most 0x0F for real ids, so it sorts after every real key, even a +NaN z of 0xFFFFFFFF. Every barrier is then trivially uniform. -0 is normalized with integer operations through bounds read as vec4u. The draw args are reset every frame. The 7 uniform slices go out in one writeBuffer per frame. Costs: nothing exits early, so every frame sorts N_pad = ceil(transparentCount/1024)*1024 elements, even when only a few are visible. There are 22 dispatches. The scan column walk makes 98 serial load/store steps per pass with in-place writes, which limits load hoisting, so its ~13 us/pass estimate is optimistic. It reads 8 B vec2u keys in count. The design's own worst-case estimate is ~0.9 ms, a thin margin against 1 ms. With all z equal, count also makes a 1024-way LDS atomicAdd on a single bin. The CPU model mirrors the kernels phase by phase (one lane loop per barrier) and runs good oracle/shuffle/LSD-invariant tests. It has no race checker, and the GPU check reads back only the final order, so a divergence is not traced to a stage.

scores.name: bandwidth
scores.notes: It is the most ambitious design, and the algorithm appears correct. Budgets check out: storage entries are 7 and 5 (within 8); workgroup memory is 10332, 8200 and 10248 B, all within 16384. The ballot ranking is the same stable popcount scheme, with barriers a/b/d/f placed correctly. The global scan is redundant per workgroup, summing the 25 rows, so there is no look-back. The w1 packing (17-bit slot | id[0:15) << 17) and the 8/7/5 split are right, and so are the trivial-digit test (max(d) + max(MASK^d) == MASK) and the parity cur(p) = popcount(nt & ((1<<p)-2)) & 1. Params are override constants, so the writeBuffer gotcha cannot occur. But the design carries a lot of data-dependent machinery: 14 pipelines, GPU-decided pass skipping, dynamic ping-pong parity, a dynamic emitting pass, an identity-emit special case in PASS 6, a fused two-half gather, and a P2 re-fetch of entity-ids. The control flow therefore changes from frame to frame, which multiplies the states to test and makes GPU/CPU divergences harder to localize. Risks: nothing clears the args when T == 0, so correctness depends on ForwardPass also skipping the draw (a stale redraw otherwise). The private arrays w0[16] and w1[16] are indexed by round with a runtime bound and will likely spill to scratch on AMD. With only 25 workgroups of 16 serial rounds each (48+ barriers) on about 12 CUs, the kernels risk being latency-bound, so the 16.4 MB / ~0.2-0.35 ms figure is likely optimistic. Mask clears must be atomicStore (not stated). The packing hard-codes MAX_ENTITIES <= 2^17. Its best ideas are worth grafting, but as the base design it is the hardest to verify.

grafts: From bandwidth: SoA key words inside ONE buffer per ping-pong side (lo[CAP] then hi[CAP], at offsets) instead of array<vec2u>. The upsweep then reads only the 4 B word its digit lives in (about -0.4 MB per pass), and the binding count stays at 6: splitting into separate lo/hi bindings would reach the 8-storage limit.

From bandwidth: lane-privatized upsweep histograms (8 copies selected by lid & 7, 8 KB). With all z equal, passes 3..6 otherwise make 1024-way serialized LDS atomicAdd on a single bin per tile, and that case is the common 2D one.

From bandwidth: the final pass writes only slots into transparent-order. Keys are written in pass 6 only in dev/readback builds, selected by an override constant (for example WRITE_KEYS), which saves about 0.8 MB at 100k. Keep keys-b for the per-stage readback in dev.

From bandwidth: have the gather record per-digit min/max (atomicMax of d and of MASK^d into the state header, which clearBuffer or writeBuffer zeroes). Expose it in the dev readback so the digitBase checks can also assert which passes were trivial. Skip trivial passes only as a measured later optimization, not in v1.

From bandwidth: set minBindingSize on EVERY storage layout entry (state 64, hist 7236, key/val sizes), not only on the uniforms, so a size mismatch fails at bind-group creation instead of at dispatch time.

From bandwidth, as a documented fallback if the profiler shows dispatch overhead dominating: fold the scan into the scatter with redundant per-workgroup row sums (bounded because the tile count is capped). That removes 7 dispatches without any cross-workgroup dependency.

From simplicity: send the per-frame uniform data (GatherParams, plus the args/diag reset if it is kept as writeBuffer) in as few writes as possible, and pin in a mock-device test that execute() issues no writeBuffer. Keep the explicit rejected-alternatives list: a last-workgroup scan needs a device-scope fence WGSL lacks, onesweep needs forward progress, and the in-tile bitonic/1-bit split needs 36-128 barriers.

From simplicity: the test that non-empty Light2D regions 26/27 (and the opaque 0..13) are excluded, with populated inputs rather than merely unread slots, plus the LSD-invariant check after every pass.

Fix in the winner: the '22 bind groups' text should read 8 (1 gather + 7 sort). Validate the uniformity of the read-only-storage early exit (getCompilationInfo plus an error-scoped createComputePipeline on the AMD adapter) before writing the rest; otherwise switch to lid0 -> workgroup var -> workgroupUniformLoad from the start.

scores.name: bandwidth
scores.notes: I found nothing incorrect. Storage counts are 7 for the gather layout and 5 for the sort layout. Workgroup memory is at most 10,332 B. The digit packing checks out: w1 = slot(17 bits) | id[0:15)<<17, so P0 = (w1>>17)&0xFF and P1 = w1>>25. The slot fits in 17 bits because renderer.ts:56 hardcodes MAX_ENTITIES = 100_000. The ballot-popcount rank plus the per-round bucketBase += cnt_b is a true stable counting sort. The trivial-digit test max(d) + max(MASK^d) == MASK is exact. Skipping a constant digit is an identity, so the parity popcount(nt & ((1<<p)-2)) and the lastNT emit are right. All early exits go through workgroupUniformLoad. There is no cross-workgroup wait, because each scatter sums all rows written by the previous dispatch. Per-pass values are override constants, so the writeBuffer gotcha cannot occur. It moves the fewest bytes: 16.4 MB worst case, about 5.6 MB for typical 2D where the 4 z passes are skipped. It also coalesces writes best: 4096-element tiles give runs of about 16 elements per digit, and 25x256 active lines fit in L2. Weaknesses: (1) At 100k only 25 workgroups run, about half the iGPU's resident slots, and each one serialises 16 rounds of 3 barriers. (2) w0[16]/w1[16] are indexed inside a loop with a runtime trip count, which risks spilling to scratch. It should loop to a constant 16 with a uniform guard. (3) When T == 0 it neither clears nor resets the state, so ForwardPass must skip the draw or it replays stale slots. The other two designs reset the args in prepare(). (4) The 8/7/5 digit widths, the entity-ids fetch in P2, parity computed on the GPU, the identity emit in PASS 6, 14 override pipelines and a data-dependent run time together give the largest special-case surface. The CPU model and the tests have to cover all of it, which is why it scores lowest on simplicity.

scores.name: simplicity
scores.notes: It is correct. Storage counts are 7 and 5; workgroup memory is 1024 B for count and scan and 9216 B for scatter. The sentinel keys (0xFFFFFFFF, 0xFFFFFFFF) sort strictly last: their id byte 2 is 0xFF, against at most 0x0F for any real id. Padding every tile to full makes every barrier trivially uniform, with no bounds checks and no reliance on uniformity analysis. Ranking is stable with 13 barriers per tile. The scan is its own 1-workgroup dispatch, so there is no forward-progress assumption. The 7 slices are written in one writeBuffer per frame, and the ping-pong parity puts the result in transparent-order. Resetting the draw args in prepare() closes the stale-args hole. The arithmetic holds: 98 tiles, N_pad = 100,352, 392 gather workgroups. Performance is its weakness. (1) It sorts the CPU bound transparentCount, which includes off-screen entities and transparent lights, with no early-out: 100k transparent entities with 1k on screen still cost the full sort. (2) The in-place column scan is a 98-deep chain of load, store and load on the same buffer that the compiler cannot reorder, about 13 us per pass and 90 us per frame. (3) count reads the whole 8-byte vec2u to use one 4-byte word. (4) The last pass writes keys nobody reads. (5) 22 dispatches is a fixed floor, and 1024-element tiles scatter into about 256x48 partial lines, more than the 2 MB L2 holds, so writes are amplified. It estimates itself at 0.45-0.9 ms worst case, a thin margin on shared-DRAM hardware. The CPU model is good: one lane loop per barrier phase and a stable-sort oracle.

scores.name: verifiability
scores.notes: It is correct and uses the same textbook reduce-then-scan algorithm as 'simplicity'. Storage counts are 7 for the gather and 6 for the sort layout, including the read-only state. Workgroup memory is 48, 1024, 1024 and 9216 B. The 52-bit key is split as lo = zKey<<20 | id and hi = zKey>>12. Passes 0-3 read lo and passes 4-6 read hi (pass 6 sees only digits 0-15). The region lookup, a count of regionEnd[q] <= i, skips empty regions correctly. Phase (c) of the scatter is sound: only the last-ranked element writes cursor, and only threads that set a mask bit clear its word. The tile guard 'if (t*1024 >= n) return' before the barriers relies on loads from var<storage, read> counting as uniform. WGSL treats read-only module-scope storage as uniform, and the design names the workgroupUniformLoad fallback. The per-pass PassParams are constants written once at setup, and the gather params once per frame, so it is the most immune to the writeBuffer gotcha. Working from the GPU count n (clamped to L, with an overflow flag) means off-screen transparent entities cost nothing, unlike 'simplicity'. Chunking the scan into 8 loads cuts the latency chain from 98 round trips to about 13. It has the strongest verification story: a phase simulator that runs threads and workgroups in shuffled order, a race checker on workgroup memory, digitBase kept per pass, diag bits, and a per-stage GPU readback compared word for word with the CPU model. That matters because WGSL cannot run headless. Weaknesses: it says '22 bind groups', but there are 8 (1 + 7). Keys are stored AoS as vec2, so upsweep reads 8 B per element. The final pass still writes keys-b, which only the dev readback needs. There are 22 dispatches, and the dev MAP_READ ring and the debug API add TypeScript surface. The same 1024-tile write-coalescing limit applies as in 'simplicity'. Its estimate is 0.35-0.8 ms at 100k.

grafts: From bandwidth: store the key as SoA words (zKey-hi and lo/id in separate arrays) so each upsweep reads only the 4-byte word its digit lives in. That saves about 0.4 MB per pass at 100k.
From bandwidth: the final radix pass writes only the slots to transparent-order. Writing keys-b becomes dev-only, behind the readback, which saves about 0.8 MB per frame.

From bandwidth: privatize the upsweep histogram per lane, with 8 copies selected by lid & 7 (8 KB). With skewed digits (all z = 0, a pass-6 digit of at most 16 values) at most 4-8 lanes then contend per wave instead of 32-64.

From bandwidth: as a measured follow-up, skip trivial digits. atomicMax of d and of MASK^d is taken in gather and upsweep, and a constant digit is an identity pass. In the common 2D case (z = 0) that removes the 4 z passes. It needs the GPU-side parity or lastNT emit, so it should come only after the profiler justifies it. A cheaper first step, from simplicity: skip the id-high pass using a CPU-known id high-water mark, with a fixed output buffer so the parity never moves.
From bandwidth: fuse pass 0 into the gather (a histogram half, then a scatter half), so the unsorted list is never written and one full read and write of the keys is saved.

From bandwidth: evaluate larger tiles (2048/4096 as 8/16 rounds of 256). Per-digit runs get longer and fewer partial write lines stay live at once (tiles x 256 against the 2 MB L2), which reduces write amplification in the scatter. Measure it with the transparent-sort/scatter stage.

From bandwidth: set minBindingSize on EVERY layout entry (state 64, hist 7236, key and value arrays at full size), and keep workgroupUniformLoad of n as the documented fallback if Tint or the AMD path rejects the guard that relies on read-only storage being uniform.

From simplicity: one constants module (TILE, ROUNDS, RADIX, PASS_TABLE, FIRST_TRANSPARENT_ARG = 14, GATHER_REGIONS = 12), imported by TransparentSortPass, the CPU model and the WGSL text-agreement tests. Also keep the rule that every barrier-separated WGSL phase is one lane loop in TypeScript.

From simplicity: keep resetting the draw args in prepare() every frame AND have ForwardPass skip the draw on transparentCount == 0, belt and braces against replaying stale indirect args (bandwidth's T == 0 path lacks this).
Fix verifiability's doc slip: there are 8 bind groups (1 gather + 7 sort), not 22.

runnersUp.name: bandwidth
runnersUp.summary: The design makes 14 direct dispatches, and all of them use one digit order: 7 stable LSD passes over a 52-bit logical key (zKey << 20 | id), with digit widths 8,7,5,8,8,8,8. The digit boundaries sit where the element packing changes. Each element takes 8 bytes and is stored SoA in two words: w0 = zKey, and w1 = slot (17 bits) | id[0:15) << 17. The two id-high digits (id bits 15-19) are fetched from entity-ids[slot] only in pass P2, and that pass is skipped while every visible id is below 32768. The gather is fused into pass 0 in two halves. gather_hist reads only visible-indices and entity-ids, and it builds the per-tile P0 histograms, the per-digit min/max and the draw args. gather_scatter then gathers bounds.z and scatters the elements straight into P0-sorted order, so the unsorted list is never written. The draw args are indexCount 6, instanceCount V, and first instance 0. Stable in-tile ranking is portable without subgroups. For each round of 256 elements, every lane sets its bit in workgroup-memory ballot masks: 256 buckets x 8 u32 words, one word per 32 lanes, set with atomicOr. A lane's rank is the popcount of same-digit bits below its lane index, so it depends only on the element's index and never on atomic order. There is no chained scan and no look-back. Each scatter workgroup redundantly sums the tile-histogram rows (25 rows at 100k), prefix over earlier tiles and total over all tiles, then runs a 256-wide exclusive scan in workgroup memory. Per-pass parameters are override constants, so no uniform is ever rewritten inside a frame. The data-dependent state lives on the GPU in an 80-byte state buffer: V, which digits are trivial (from atomicMax of d and of ~d), the ping-pong parity, and which pass emits. A pass whose digit is constant exits in its prologue. The last non-trivial pass writes slots (4 B) straight into 'transparent-sorted' instead of elements (8 B). Worst case at 100k moves about 16.4 MB, which is about 0.16-0.27 ms of DRAM time plus about 40-70 us of dispatch overhead. The common 2D case (all z = 0, ids < 32768) runs only P0 and P1, about 5.6 MB and about 0.1 ms.

kernels.name: gather_hist (transparent-gather.wgsl)
kernels.dispatch: dispatchWorkgroups(N), with N = ceil(min(transparentCount, 100000) / 4096), between 1 and 25, from the CPU upper bound. On the GPU, V = min(sum of the 12 instanceCounts of buckets 14..25, frame.maxCount). A workgroup t with t*4096 >= V exits uniformly, but workgroup 0 writes the draw args first.
bindings: @group(0) @binding(0) frame: uniform SortFrame {maxCount, _pad0, _pad1, _pad2}, 16 B; read
@binding(1) drawArgsIn = 'indirect-args' as array<u32>, read-only storage; the counts are at [(14+r)*5+1] for r in 0..11
@binding(2) visibleIndices = 'visible-indices' array<u32>, read-only storage; read
@binding(3) entityIds = 'entity-ids' array<u32>, read-only storage; read
@binding(4) bounds = 'entity-bounds' array<vec4f>, read-only storage; not used by this entry point, still counted (shared layout)
@binding(5) tileHist array<u32>, storage read_write; writes row t (256 u32)
@binding(6) elems array<u32>, storage read_write; not used here, still counted

@binding(7) state SortState, storage read_write, 20 u32: [0..5) DrawIndexedIndirect args, [5..12) digitMax (atomic), [12..19) digitInvMax (atomic), [19] flags; writes the args and flags, atomicMax on the 3 id digits
kernels.algorithm:
Workgroup memory: hist atomic<u32>[256] (1024 B), regionStart u32[13] (52 B), wgMax/wgInv for digits P0-P2 (24 B), wgV (4 B).
(1) Every lane zeroes hist[lid]; lanes lid < 6 zero wgMax and wgInv. Lane 0 reads the 12 counts c_r = drawArgsIn[(14+r)*5+1] and writes regionStart[0..12] as an exclusive prefix, with regionStart[12] = sum. It sets wgV = min(sum, frame.maxCount). If workgroup_id == 0, it also writes state.indexCount = 6 and state.instanceCount = V (firstIndex, baseVertex and firstInstance stay 0 from the per-frame clearBuffer), and sets flags bit0 when sum > maxCount (a dev overflow signal).
(2) V = workgroupUniformLoad(&wgV), which is also a barrier. If t*4096 >= V, return; the condition is uniform.
(3) For each of 16 rounds r (a constant-trip loop, no barriers inside): i = t*4096 + r*256 + lid. If i < V: region = the number of k in 1..11 with i >= regionStart[k]; slot = visibleIndices[(14+region)*100000 + i - regionStart[region]]; id = entityIds[slot]; atomicAdd(&hist[id & 0xFF], 1). The lane also keeps register max(d) and max(MASK ^ d) for d0 = id & 0xFF, d1 = (id >> 8) & 0x7F and d2 = (id >> 15) & 0x1F.
(4) Each lane that saw at least one element does atomicMax into wgMax[q] and wgInv[q]. workgroupBarrier.
(5) tileHist[t*256 + lid] = atomicLoad(&hist[lid]), a dense row that includes zeros. Lanes lid < 3 do atomicMax(&state.digitMax[lid]) and atomicMax(&state.digitInvMax[lid]).
This kernel only counts, so atomic order cannot affect the result, and the global maxima are order-independent.

kernels.name: gather_scatter = radix pass P0 (transparent-gather.wgsl)
kernels.dispatch: The same N and the same early exit as gather_hist. It is a separate dispatch because it needs every tile's P0 row. Writes elems half 0.
bindings: same layout as gather_hist:
@binding(0) frame uniform; read
@binding(1) drawArgsIn read-only storage; read
@binding(2) visibleIndices read-only storage; read
@binding(3) entityIds read-only storage; read
@binding(4) bounds read-only storage; reads .z
@binding(5) tileHist storage read_write (declared read_write to match the layout); only reads rows
@binding(6) elems storage read_write; writes half 0: w0 at [0*CAP + dst], w1 at [1*CAP + dst]
@binding(7) state storage read_write; atomicMax on digits P3-P6
kernels.algorithm:
Workgroup memory: masks atomic<u32>[256*8] (8192 B), bucketBase u32[256] (1024), scanTmp u32[256] (1024), regionStart[13] (52), zMax/zInv for 4 digits (32), wgV and wgRounds (8).
(1) The prologue matches gather_hist: regionStart, then V through workgroupUniformLoad, then the uniform exit. rounds = min(16, ceil((V - t*4096)/256)) and numTiles = ceil(V/4096) are uniform.
(2) Bases, with lane = bucket b: for k < numTiles, h = tileHist[k*256+b]; total += h; if k < t, prefix += h. Then a Hillis-Steele exclusive scan of total over the 256 lanes in scanTmp (8 steps, each a read, workgroupBarrier, add, workgroupBarrier). bucketBase[b] = excl(b) + prefix. Each lane zeroes masks[b*8 .. b*8+7]. workgroupBarrier.
(3) Loads, all issued before any ranking so memory latency is paid once. For r < rounds: i = t*4096 + r*256 + lid; valid = i < V. slot comes from the region lookup as in gather_hist; id = entityIds[slot]; zb = bitcast<u32>(bounds[slot].z); if zb == 0x80000000 then zb = 0 (-0 becomes +0); w0[r] = zb ^ select(0x80000000, 0xFFFFFFFF, (zb >> 31) != 0); w1[r] = slot | ((id & 0x7FFF) << 17). The lane updates its register max and invMax for the 4 z bytes.
(4) Rank rounds, r < rounds, loop bound uniform:
  a. If valid: d = (w1[r] >> 17) & 0xFF; atomicOr(&masks[d*8 + (lid >> 5)], 1u << (lid & 31)).
  b. workgroupBarrier.
  c. If valid: rank = sum over k < lid>>5 of countOneBits(masks[d*8+k]) + countOneBits(masks[d*8 + (lid>>5)] & ((1u << (lid & 31)) - 1u)); dst = bucketBase[d] + rank; elems[dst] = w0[r]; elems[CAP + dst] = w1[r]. Lane b also computes cnt_b = sum over k < 8 of countOneBits(masks[b*8+k]).
  d. workgroupBarrier, so every rank read is done.
  e. bucketBase[b] += cnt_b; masks[b*8 .. b*8+7] = 0.
  f. workgroupBarrier.
(5) z digits: each lane does atomicMax into zMax and zInv. workgroupBarrier. Lanes lid < 4 do atomicMax into state.digitMax[3+lid] and state.digitInvMax[3+lid].
Why it is stable: dst = (elements with a smaller digit) + (same digit in earlier tiles) + (same digit in earlier rounds) + (same digit at a lower lane in this round). That is exactly the number of elements ordered before this one in a stable counting sort. atomicOr is commutative, so the masks, and with them the ranks, are the same whatever order the atomics run in.

kernels.name: digit_hist, override PASS = 1..6 (6 pipelines, transparent-sort.wgsl)
kernels.dispatch: dispatchWorkgroups(N), same N. A workgroup exits uniformly when its tile is at or past ceil(V/4096), or when digit PASS is trivial.
bindings: @group(0) @binding(0) state SortStateView, plain u32 view of the same 80 B, read-only storage: V = instanceCount, digitMax, digitInvMax
@binding(1) elems storage read_write (layout match); reads only the word the digit needs, from half cur
@binding(2) entityIds read-only storage; PASS 2 only (id bits 15-19)
@binding(3) tileHist storage read_write; writes row t
@binding(4) sortedSlots = 'transparent-sorted' storage read_write; not used here, still counted
kernels.algorithm:
Workgroup memory: hist atomic<u32>[8*256] (8192 B, 8 lane-privatized copies selected by lid & 7, so a skewed digit serializes at most 4-8 lanes per wave instruction instead of 32-64), plus wgV and wgNt (8).
(1) Each lane zeroes 8 hist words. Lane 0 reads V and, for q = 0..6, sets trivial_q when digitMax[q] + digitInvMax[q] == (1 << BITS[q]) - 1, i.e. max == min. It stores nt = the non-trivial bits among 1..6 in wgNt.
(2) V and nt through workgroupUniformLoad, which is also the barrier. If (nt >> PASS) & 1 == 0, or t*4096 >= V, return; uniform.
(3) cur = countOneBits(nt & ((1u << PASS) - 2u)) & 1. Base of the source word: (2*cur + k) * CAP.
(4) For r < rounds, loads issued first, no barriers: when valid, d = digit(PASS). PASS 1: w1 >> 25 (7 bits). PASS 2: entityIds[w1 & 0x1FFFF] >> 15 (5 bits). PASS 3-6: (w0 >> (8*(PASS-3))) & 0xFF, which reads only the w0 array. Then atomicAdd(&hist[(lid & 7)*256 + d], 1).
(5) workgroupBarrier. tileHist[t*256 + lid] = the sum over c < 8 of hist[c*256 + lid], a dense row.

kernels.name: digit_scatter, override PASS = 1..6 (6 pipelines, transparent-sort.wgsl)
kernels.dispatch: dispatchWorkgroups(N), same N. Exits uniformly on a trivial digit or an empty tile, except PASS 6 when every pass 1..6 is trivial: then it emits in identity order.
bindings: same layout as digit_hist:
@binding(0) state read-only storage; read
@binding(1) elems storage read_write; reads half cur (both words), writes half cur^1
@binding(2) entityIds read-only storage; PASS 2 digit fetch
@binding(3) tileHist storage read_write (layout match); reads rows
@binding(4) sortedSlots storage read_write; written only by the emitting pass
kernels.algorithm:
Workgroup memory: masks atomic<u32>[2048] (8192 B), bucketBase[256] (1024), scanTmp[256] (1024), wgV and wgNt (8).
(1) Prologue as in digit_hist, giving V, nt and cur. lastNT = firstLeadingBit(nt), or 0 when nt == 0.
(2) If PASS == 6 and nt == 0, emit in identity order: for i in the tile, sortedSlots[i] = elems[CAP + i] & 0x1FFFF, reading half 0 word 1; return. This covers V == 1, ids that all differ only in bits 0-7 while z is constant, and stale ids that happen to be equal.
(3) If bit PASS of nt is 0, or the tile is empty, return; uniform.
(4) Bases exactly as in gather_scatter: row sums over numTiles give prefix (rows < t) and total; Hillis-Steele exclusive scan (16 barriers); bucketBase; clear masks; barrier.
(5) Load w0[r] and w1[r] from half cur for all rounds; for PASS 2, also idHi = entityIds[w1 & 0x1FFFF] >> 15.
(6) Rank rounds a-f, identical to gather_scatter, with d = digit(PASS). The write: if PASS == lastNT, sortedSlots[dst] = w1 & 0x1FFFF (4 B); otherwise elems[(2*(cur^1))*CAP + dst] = w0 and elems[(2*(cur^1)+1)*CAP + dst] = w1.
Every barrier is at workgroup scope and in uniform control flow: loops bounded by the uniform rounds and numTiles, lane guards (valid) only around barrier-free code, exits only on workgroup_id and values from workgroupUniformLoad. Skipped passes are identity permutations, so skipping one keeps the invariant: after pass p the order is lexicographic by (digit p .. digit 0). The final order is therefore ascending (zKey, id): far first, and at equal z the higher id last.

buffers: 'entity-ids' (new, ResourcePool): MAX_ENTITIES*4 = 400,000 B, STORAGE|COPY_DST. One u32 external id per slot, uploaded whole only on frames where the slot-to-id mapping changed, from the same GPURenderState as the SoA.

'transparent-elems' (private): 2 halves x 2 words x CAP x 4 B = 1,600,000 B, STORAGE, with CAP = 100,000. Word k of half h starts at u32 index (2h+k)*CAP. SoA, so a hist pass reads only the word its digit lives in (a true 4 B per element, not 8). Needs no clear: [0, V) is always fully written before it is read.

'transparent-tile-hist' (private): ceil(CAP/4096) = 25 rows x 256 x 4 B = 25,600 B, STORAGE. One buffer reused by every pass: each hist dispatch overwrites rows [0, numTiles) densely, before its scatter reads them. Needs no clear.

'transparent-draw-args' = sort state (ResourcePool, read by ForwardPass drawIndexedIndirect at offset 0): 20 u32 = 80 B, STORAGE|INDIRECT|COPY_DST. [0..5) is DrawIndexedIndirect {indexCount 6, instanceCount V, firstIndex 0, baseVertex 0, firstInstance 0}. [5..12) digitMax[7], [12..19) digitInvMax[7] (max of MASK^d, so a buffer zeroed by clearBuffer works as an atomicMax identity for both the minimum and the maximum), [19] flags (bit 0: gathered count clamped to maxCount). encoder.clearBuffer(0, 80) once per frame, before the first dispatch. firstInstance is 0, so this draw does not need 'indirect-first-instance'.
'transparent-sorted' (ResourcePool, ForwardPass uber-pipeline group-0 binding 2): CAP*4 = 400,000 B, STORAGE. Sorted entity slots [0, V); entries past V are stale and never read.
uniform 'transparent-sort-frame' (private): 16 B {maxCount, _pad0, _pad1, _pad2}, UNIFORM|COPY_DST. Written once per frame in prepare(); minBindingSize 16. No implicit padding: four u32.
Read, not owned: 'indirect-args' (12 counts, read-only storage), 'visible-indices' (regions 14..25, read-only), 'entity-bounds' (.z, read-only).
Total new memory: about 2.43 MB. The graph declares reads = ['indirect-args', 'visible-indices', 'entity-bounds', 'entity-ids'] and writes = ['transparent-sorted', 'transparent-draw-args'].
runnersUp.uniformHandling: There is exactly one uniform, SortFrame {maxCount: u32, _pad0, _pad1, _pad2} (16 B, no implicit padding, covered by uniform-layout.test.ts). prepare() writes it once per frame with queue.writeBuffer, and only the two gather kernels bind it. Everything that differs between passes is a pipeline-override constant (override PASS: u32). There are 12 sort pipelines (digit_hist and digit_scatter, PASS = 1..6) plus 2 gather pipelines, 14 pipelines built once in setup(). PASS picks, through const tables folded at pipeline creation, BITS = [8,7,5,8,8,8,8], the source word (w1 for P0/P1, the entity-ids fetch for P2, w0 for P3-P6) and the shift. Everything that depends on the data is computed on the GPU from the 80-byte state buffer that earlier dispatches filled, in each kernel's prologue: V, the trivial-digit mask, the ping-pong parity cur(p) = popcount(nt & ((1<<p)-2)) & 1, and lastNT. So no buffer is ever rewritten between dispatches of one frame, and the queue.writeBuffer gotcha cannot occur by construction; nor does anything need 256-byte slices. Every value that steers control flow around a barrier is read through workgroupUniformLoad, so WGSL uniformity analysis accepts the early exits. minBindingSize is set on every layout entry (16 for the uniform, 80 for state, 1,600,000 for elems, 25,600 for tileHist), so a size mismatch fails at bind-group creation rather than at dispatch time.
runnersUp.countHandling: CPU side: T = transparentCount, the upper bound exported by Rust. When T == 0 the pass does nothing: no clearBuffer, no dispatch, profileStages() returns []. ForwardPass must then skip the transparent drawIndexedIndirect (it reads frame.transparentCount); otherwise the persistent state buffer would redraw last frame's slots. When T > 0: maxCount = min(T, CAP) is written to the uniform, and N = ceil(maxCount/4096) (between 1 and 25) workgroups are dispatched for each of the 14 dispatches. GPU side: every gather workgroup recomputes V = min(sum of instanceCount of buckets 14..25, maxCount) from indirect-args. Clamping to maxCount keeps every tile below ceil(V/4096), and therefore within the dispatched grid, so no pass ever reads an unwritten element. Inconsistent inputs (the GPU count above the CPU bound) drop the last elements in region order deterministically and set state.flags bit 0 for a dev readback. gather_hist workgroup 0 writes instanceCount = V before its own early exit, so V == 0 (everything culled) gives a no-op draw, and every other kernel exits in its prologue. Later kernels read V from state.instanceCount. Tiny counts: a workgroup runs only rounds = ceil((V - t*4096)/256) rounds (uniform), and lanes with i >= V take part in barriers only. With V == 1, or when every digit in passes 1..6 is constant, digit_scatter(PASS 6) emits sortedSlots in identity order from half 0, so the draw always has valid slots. Since ids are unique, V >= 2 normally makes at least one id digit non-trivial. The indirect-dispatch alternative was rejected: it would need its args written by gather_hist, and it would save only the launch of workgroups that exit within a few instructions.
runnersUp.bandwidthEstimate100k: V = 100,000, 25 tiles of 4096; DRAM upper bound, worst case with all 7 digits non-trivial. gather_hist reads visible-indices 4 B + entity-ids 4 B = 8 B/element, 0.80 MB. gather_scatter (P0) reads 4 + 4 + bounds 16 B (vec4 lines, only .z used) and writes w0 and w1, 8 B: 32 B/element, 3.20 MB. P1: hist reads w1 4 B (0.40 MB); scatter reads 8 and writes 8 (1.60 MB): 2.00 MB. P2: hist 4 + fetch 4 (0.80 MB); scatter 8 + fetch 4 + write 8 (2.00 MB): 2.80 MB. P3, P4, P5: 2.00 MB each, 6.00 MB. P6 emits: hist 0.40 + scatter reads 0.80 + writes slots 4 B (0.40): 1.60 MB. Total: 0.8 + 3.2 + 2.0 + 2.8 + 6.0 + 1.6 = 16.4 MB/frame. At 60 GB/s that is 273 us, at 100 GB/s 164 us. Add 14 dispatch boundaries at about 3-5 us each (40-70 us), so about 0.2-0.35 ms worst case, well under the 1 ms target. There is also about 4.4 MB of L1/L2-only traffic: each scatter workgroup sums 25 rows x 1 KB from a 25.6 KB buffer (25 workgroups x 25 KB x 7). The ping-pong halves are 800 KB each, so on the RDNA 3 iGPU's L2 (about 2 MB) part of the traffic above never reaches DRAM. Typical 2D (all z = 0, ids < 32768): only P0 and P1 are non-trivial, and P1 emits: 0.8 + 3.2 + (0.4 + 0.8 + 0.4) = 5.6 MB, about 56-93 us plus about 40 us for the dispatches (10 of the 14 exit in their prologue), roughly 0.1 ms. Layered 2D (a few integer z values, whose low mantissa bytes are zero): P0, P1, P5 and P6 run: 4.0 + 2.0 + 2.0 + 1.6 = 9.6 MB, about 0.1-0.16 ms plus dispatches. For comparison, the naive layout (12 B key64+slot elements, a separate gather, 3 dispatches per pass, 7 passes) moves 3.6 + 7 x 2.8 = 23.2 MB in 22 dispatches.
runnersUp.cpuReference: ts/src/render/passes/transparent-sort-reference.ts models the same algorithm on typed arrays laid out byte for byte like the GPU buffers. elems is a Uint32Array(4*CAP) with the (2h+k)*CAP offsets, tileHist a Uint32Array(25*256), state a Uint32Array(20), sortedSlots a Uint32Array(CAP). Constants shared with the WGSL are TILE = 4096, ROUNDS = 16, WG = 256, CAP, BITS = [8,7,5,8,8,8,8], the w1 packing (slot | id[0:15) << 17) and the region base 14. It exports gatherHistCPU(wid), gatherScatterCPU(wid), digitHistCPU(PASS, wid) and digitScatterCPU(PASS, wid). A driver runs them dispatch by dispatch, workgroup by workgroup, after zeroing state as the clearBuffer does. Inside a workgroup it follows the kernel's phases, with a barrier at every phase boundary. For each round it first sets the ballot bits of every valid lane in a Uint32Array(2048) (masks[d*8 + (lid >> 5)] |= 1 << (lid & 31)). It then computes each lane's rank with the same popcount prefix, each bucket's cnt_b, the bucketBase update and the clear. The bases use the same row sums, prefix for rows < t and totals over numTiles, and the exclusive scan. V comes from the 12 counts with the maxCount clamp. The region lookup counts k in 1..11. Trivial flags come from digitMax + digitInvMax == mask, then parity cur(p), lastNT, the early exits and the identity emit. floatToSortKey is kept from radix-sort-pass.ts, with -0 turned into +0 first. Oracle tests compare sortedSlots[0..V) and state[0..5) against a naive comparator sort of the gathered slots by (floatToSortKey(z), id). They cover seeded random scenes; all z equal (2D); few integer layers; negative, positive and -0 z; ids >= 32768 (exercises the P2 fetch); ids < 256; V in {1, 255, 256, 257, 4095, 4096, 4097, 100000}; empty and full regions; and the maxCount clamp. Invariance tests check that shuffling within regions, or moving entities between regions, gives the same output: the full key is unique, which is why the result is stable across frames although cull's order is not. A forced-non-trivial mode, where every pass runs, must give the same output as the skipping mode. Every non-trivial pass must be stable, and the pair (half, word) must be followed pass by pass. Text tests on the WGSL assert that its BITS, TILE, CAP, packing shifts and region constants equal the TS ones; that each layout has at most 8 storage entries, counted on the layouts setup() creates, as in cull-pass.test.ts; and that the var<workgroup> declarations sum to at most 16384 B per entry point. On the GPU, a dev readback of 'transparent-sorted' and 'transparent-draw-args' is compared with the CPU model run on the same frame's read-back inputs, alongside the 2D Twins probe check.
risks: Per-round ballot atomics serialize on skewed digits. When all 32 lanes of a group share a digit, they atomicOr the same workgroup word; that costs at most 32-way serialization x 16 rounds per workgroup, and passes whose digit is fully constant are skipped. This needs a GPU measurement with the profiler stages gather/id/z.

Occupancy at 100k is only 25 workgroups on about 12 CUs. If the kernels turn out latency-bound rather than bandwidth-bound, fall back to TILE = 2048 (49 workgroups). The row-sum prefix then doubles in L2 reads, so switch to per-pass totals built with atomicAdd.

The private arrays w0[16] and w1[16] indexed by round must be unrolled into registers. If Tint or the AMD compiler spills them to scratch, use a two-deep software pipeline instead (load round r+1 while ranking round r). Check in the RGP or Dawn output, or by timing.
The packing assumes MAX_ENTITIES <= 2^17 (the slot has 17 bits) and MAX_EXTERNAL_ID < 2^20. Pin both with a test against types.ts and renderer.ts; raising either one requires a new element layout.

'entity-ids' can be out of step with visible-indices (an upload skipped on a frame where slots moved). The result is still a valid permutation, since every radix sort is one, but ties could be ordered wrongly for that frame. Duplicate ids could make every pass trivial, and the identity emit in PASS 6 covers that case.
If ForwardPass does not skip the transparent draw when transparentCount == 0, the persistent state buffer redraws stale slots. Both sides must key off frame.transparentCount; a test should pin this.

The gather reads bounds as AoS vec4, 16 B per element for 4 useful bytes, which is the largest single cost (1.6 MB). A packed world-z column would save 1.2 MB at 100k, but cull stays untouched, so it is left for later.
Skipping trivial passes makes the running time depend on the data (0.1 to 0.35 ms). Profile both the worst case (random z, ids >= 32768) and the typical case, not only the demo scene.

Uniformity: all early exits and loop bounds come from workgroup_id, override constants or workgroupUniformLoad. A future edit that reads V straight from storage in a branch around a barrier fails WGSL compilation, which is only visible in a browser. Validate with getCompilationInfo on the dev server.

DRAM figures assume the ping-pong data spills. On the iGPU, L2 residency (about 2 MB) makes real traffic lower, but the CPU and the display compositor share LPDDR5 bandwidth, so the measured time can vary between frames.

Rejected alternatives, recorded so they are not retried. 11-bit digits (5 passes): ballot masks would need 64 KB, and 2048-bucket histograms force a separate scan dispatch. Onesweep look-back: requires forward progress across workgroups. Atomics that build the next pass's histogram: hot global addresses on skewed digits. 12 B key+slot elements: +0.8 MB per pass. A 4 MB id-to-slot map: random traffic. Indirect dispatch: it would itself need its args written by an earlier dispatch, and it saves only a few microseconds.

runnersUp.name: simplicity
runnersUp.summary: 'simplicity' is the textbook reduce-then-scan LSD radix sort with 4 entry points: gather, count, scan and scatter. Every size is fixed or comes from the CPU. The key is a vec2u (x = external id, y = sortable z). It is sorted in 7 passes of 8-bit digits, id word first (bits 0-7, 8-15, 16-23), then the z word (0, 8, 16, 24). A tile is 1024 elements, handled by a 256-thread workgroup as 4 in-order rounds of 256 lanes. Stable ranking inside a round needs neither subgroups nor sorting networks. Each lane sets its bit in a per-digit 256-bit lane mask in workgroup memory (atomicOr), and its rank is the popcount of the same-digit lanes below it. A per-digit cursor carries the order from one round to the next. Per pass, a 1-workgroup SCAN dispatch turns the per-tile histograms into per-(tile, digit) offsets plus a base row. Dispatch boundaries are the only cross-workgroup sync. There are no global atomics anywhere in the sort, no look-back and no last-workgroup trick. The CPU bound transparentCount sets the element count, which is padded to whole tiles with max-key sentinels. So no kernel has a bounds check, every barrier is trivially in uniform control flow, and the GPU-only actual count reaches only the draw args, which the gather writes. The pass parameters are 7 uniform 256-byte slices, written once per frame. The 7 ping-pong bind groups and all buffers are created once at the 100k maximum, so there is no grow path. The CPU reference is the same 4 functions, with one lane loop per barrier-separated phase, checked against a JS stable-sort oracle. Rejected alternatives: in-tile bitonic sort or 1-bit splits (36-128 barriers per round against 3); scan fused into scatter (quadratic redundant reads); last-workgroup scan (WGSL has no device-scope fence); onesweep (needs forward progress); indirect dispatch (not needed once padded).

kernels.name: gather (ts/src/shaders/transparent-gather.wgsl, entry 'gather')
kernels.dispatch: CPU: numTiles*ROUNDS = N_pad/256 workgroups, where N = min(transparentCount, 100000), numTiles = ceil(N/1024), N_pad = numTiles*1024. At 100k: 392 workgroups. Skipped entirely when N == 0.
bindings: @group(0) @binding(0) params: var<uniform> SortParams (slice 0 of tsort-params: numTiles, regionSize), read
@group(0) @binding(1) args: var<storage, read> array<u32> = 'indirect-args' (instanceCount of slot s at s*5+1), read
@group(0) @binding(2) visible: var<storage, read> array<u32> = 'visible-indices', read
@group(0) @binding(3) boundsBits: var<storage, read> array<vec4u> = 'entity-bounds' read as BITS (.z = world z), read
@group(0) @binding(4) ids: var<storage, read> array<u32> = 'entity-ids' (slot -> external id), read
@group(0) @binding(5) keysOut: var<storage, read_write> array<vec2u> = tsort-keys-a, write
@group(0) @binding(6) valsOut: var<storage, read_write> array<u32> = tsort-vals-a, write
@group(0) @binding(7) drawArgs: var<storage, read_write> array<u32, 5> = 'transparent-draw-args', write (thread 0 only)
kernels.algorithm: Thread i = global_invocation_id.x, i in [0, N_pad). (1) Region prefix, computed by each thread in a uniform loop k = 0..11 (GATHER_REGIONS = 12, FIRST_TRANSPARENT_ARG = 14, so args slots 14..25; Light2D slots 26/27 are never read): c = min(args[(14+k)*5+1], P.regionSize); if (i >= start && i < start + c) { region = k; local = i - start; } start += c. The 12 loads have uniform addresses (scalar/K$ hits). n = min(start, P.numTiles*1024). (2) if (i == 0u): drawArgs = [6, n, 0, 0, 0] (indexCount, instanceCount, firstIndex, baseVertex, firstInstance = 0, so no indirect-first-instance dependency). (3) if (i < n): slot = visible[(14+region)*P.regionSize + local]; zb = boundsBits[slot].z; if (zb == 0x80000000u) { zb = 0u; } (-0.0 becomes +0.0 with integer ops only; a float 'z + 0.0' can be folded by the driver, since Vulkan does not guarantee signed-zero preservation, and a float load could flush a denormal); zKey = zb ^ select(0x80000000u, 0xFFFFFFFFu, (zb >> 31u) == 1u) (the floatToSortKey mapping); keysOut[i] = vec2u(ids[slot], zKey); valsOut[i] = slot. else (padding, n <= i < N_pad): keysOut[i] = vec2u(0xFFFFFFFFu, 0xFFFFFFFFu); valsOut[i] = 0u. A sentinel is strictly greater than every real key on the 56 sorted bits: its id-byte-2 digit is 0xFF against <= 0x0F for ids <= 1_048_575, and its z word is 0xFFFFFFFF. Padding also comes after every real element in input order, so it sorts to [n, N_pad) and is never drawn. No barriers, no atomics. Every element of [0, N_pad) is written, so nothing needs clearing. The output is in cull's nondeterministic region order, which does not matter because the full (z, id) key is unique.

kernels.name: count (ts/src/shaders/radix-sort.wgsl rewritten, entry 'count')
kernels.dispatch: CPU: numTiles workgroups (98 at 100k), once per radix pass p = 0..6, with bindGroup[p].
bindings: @group(0) @binding(0) P: var<uniform> SortParams (slice p: numTiles, keyWord, shift), read
@group(0) @binding(1) srcKeys: var<storage, read> array<vec2u>, read
@group(0) @binding(2) srcVals: var<storage, read> array<u32>, in the shared layout, unused here
@group(0) @binding(3) dstKeys: var<storage, read_write> array<vec2u>, in the shared layout, unused here
@group(0) @binding(4) dstVals: var<storage, read_write> array<u32>, in the shared layout, unused here
@group(0) @binding(5) hist: var<storage, read_write> array<u32> = tsort-hist, write row t
kernels.algorithm: Tile t = workgroup_id.x covers elements [t*1024, t*1024 + 1024). Workgroup memory: localHist: array<atomic<u32>, 256>. (1) atomicStore(&localHist[lid], 0u); workgroupBarrier(). (2) for (r = 0; r < ROUNDS(4); r++) (constant bound): k = srcKeys[t*1024 + r*256 + lid]; atomicAdd(&localHist[(k[P.keyWord] >> P.shift) & 0xFFu], 1u). (3) workgroupBarrier(); hist[t*256 + lid] = atomicLoad(&localHist[lid]) (thread lid writes the count of digit lid, coalesced 1 KB row). Two barriers, both at top level. The atomics race, but addition commutes, so the row is deterministic. Rows 0..numTiles-1 are fully rewritten every pass, so no clearBuffer is needed. No bounds check: padding makes every tile full.

kernels.name: scan (radix-sort.wgsl, entry 'scan')
kernels.dispatch: CPU: exactly 1 workgroup, once per radix pass, with bindGroup[p].
bindings: @group(0) @binding(0) P: var<uniform> SortParams (numTiles), read
@group(0) @binding(1..4): the shared-layout key/value buffers, unused here
@group(0) @binding(5) hist: var<storage, read_write> array<u32> = tsort-hist, read+write in place, plus the base row at index numTiles
kernels.algorithm: Thread d owns digit d. (1) Along the tiles, in place: sum = 0; for (t = 0; t < P.numTiles; t++) { c = hist[t*256 + d]; hist[t*256 + d] = sum; sum += c; }. Row t then holds #{elements of digit d in tiles < t}. Each thread touches only its own column, so this needs no barrier, and each step reads one contiguous 1 KB row (coalesced, L2-resident). (2) Across the digits: scanTmp[d] = sum; workgroupBarrier(); then a Hillis-Steele inclusive scan in 8 steps, off = 1, 2, 4 .. 128 (constant loop): var v = 0u; if (d >= off) { v = scanTmp[d - off]; } workgroupBarrier(); scanTmp[d] += v; workgroupBarrier(). (3) hist[P.numTiles*256 + d] = scanTmp[d] - sum. This is the exclusive base row: #{elements with digit < d}. 17 barriers, all in uniform control flow; the only non-uniform branch holds no barrier. This single-workgroup dispatch is the whole global scan. The count -> scan -> scatter dispatch boundaries are the only cross-workgroup synchronisation, so there is no forward-progress or device-fence assumption.

kernels.name: scatter (radix-sort.wgsl, entry 'scatter')
kernels.dispatch: CPU: numTiles workgroups (98 at 100k), once per radix pass, with bindGroup[p]. Pass 6 writes dstVals = 'transparent-order'.
bindings: @group(0) @binding(0) P: var<uniform> SortParams (slice p: numTiles, keyWord, shift), read
@group(0) @binding(1) srcKeys: var<storage, read> array<vec2u>, read
@group(0) @binding(2) srcVals: var<storage, read> array<u32>, read
@group(0) @binding(3) dstKeys: var<storage, read_write> array<vec2u>, write
@group(0) @binding(4) dstVals: var<storage, read_write> array<u32>, write
@group(0) @binding(5) hist: var<storage, read_write> array<u32> (declared read_write to match the shared layout), read row t and the base row
kernels.algorithm: Tile t = workgroup_id.x, lane l = local_invocation_index. Workgroup memory: masks: array<atomic<u32>, 2048> (256 digits x 8 words = one bit per lane of a 256-lane round, 8192 B) and cursor: array<u32, 256> (1024 B). (0) Thread d: cursor[d] = hist[P.numTiles*256 + d] + hist[t*256 + d]; clears masks[d*8 .. d*8+7]. workgroupBarrier (B0). for (r = 0; r < 4; r++) (constant bound, so the barriers are uniform): (A) i = t*1024 + r*256 + l; k = srcKeys[i]; v = srcVals[i]; d = (k[P.keyWord] >> P.shift) & 0xFFu; atomicOr(&masks[d*8 + (l >> 5u)], 1u << (l & 31u)); workgroupBarrier (B1: the round's masks are complete). (B) rank = countOneBits(atomicLoad(&masks[d*8 + (l>>5)]) & ((1u << (l & 31u)) - 1u)); for (w = 0; w < (l>>5); w++) { rank += countOneBits(atomicLoad(&masks[d*8 + w])); } (non-uniform loop bound, no barrier inside); dst = cursor[d] + rank; dstKeys[dst] = k; dstVals[dst] = v; workgroupBarrier (B2: every lane has read the masks and cursors). (C) Thread d (as digit owner): cnt = the sum over w = 0..7 of countOneBits(atomicLoad(&masks[d*8+w])), then clears those 8 words; cursor[d] += cnt; workgroupBarrier (B3: masks clear and cursors advanced for round r+1). 13 barriers per tile. STABILITY: element i = t*1024 + r*256 + l with digit d lands at base[d] + #{digit d in tiles < t} (scan) + #{digit d in earlier rounds of this tile} (cursor) + #{digit d in lanes < l of this round} (popcount) = base[d] + #{j < i : digit(e_j) = d}. That is the definition of a stable counting sort, and it needs no ordering assumption: lane order is input order by construction of i. The only atomics are atomicOr on workgroup memory, which commutes, so the permutation is bit-identical under any scheduling. Contention: at equal digits (all sprites at z = 0), one wave's 32 lanes OR the same word, at most 32-way serialised, about 256 LDS cycles per round, which is negligible.

buffers: tsort-params: UNIFORM|COPY_DST, 7 * 256 = 1792 B. Slice p at offset p*256 holds SortParams {numTiles, keyWord, shift, regionSize} (16 B). The gather binds slice 0. Written by one writeBuffer in prepare(), once per frame.
tsort-keys-a: STORAGE, MAX_SORT_ELEMS * 8 B = 100,352 * 8 = 802,816 B, array<vec2u> (x = id, y = zKey). Written by the gather; ping-pong side 0.
tsort-keys-b: STORAGE, 802,816 B. Ping-pong side 1.
tsort-vals-a: STORAGE, MAX_SORT_ELEMS * 4 = 401,408 B, array<u32> of entity slot indices. Written by the gather; ping-pong side 0.

transparent-order (published in the ResourcePool; it is also ping-pong vals side 1): STORAGE, 401,408 B. After pass 6 (7 passes, an odd count, so the result lands in side 1) [0, n) holds the slots back-to-front. ForwardPass's uber pipeline binds it at group-0 binding 2.

tsort-hist: STORAGE, (MAX_SORT_TILES + 1) * 256 * 4 = 99 * 1024 = 101,376 B. Rows 0..numTiles-1 hold the per-tile digit counts, then the in-place offsets; row numTiles is the base row. Fully rewritten every pass, never cleared.

transparent-draw-args (published): STORAGE|INDIRECT|COPY_DST, 20 B, the DrawIndexedIndirect args {6, n, 0, 0, 0}. prepare() writes {6,0,0,0,0} every frame, so a skipped frame draws nothing; on a sorted frame the gather's thread 0 overwrites it.
entity-ids (decided, new): STORAGE|COPY_DST, 100,000 * 4 = 400,000 B, slot -> external id. Uploaded whole only when the slot mapping changed.

Constants: MAX_SORT_TILES = ceil(100000/1024) = 98, MAX_SORT_ELEMS = 98*1024 = 100,352. Everything is allocated once in setup() at the maximum, so there is no grow path, and the 8 bind groups (1 gather + 7 passes) plus ForwardPass's bind group are built once. About 2.9 MB new in total, including entity-ids.
runnersUp.uniformHandling: One struct: SortParams { numTiles: u32, keyWord: u32, shift: u32, regionSize: u32 }. It is 16 B of four u32 with no implicit padding; uniform-layout.test.ts picks it up automatically through its ./*.wgsl glob. The struct is declared identically in transparent-gather.wgsl and radix-sort.wgsl. One 1792-byte UNIFORM|COPY_DST buffer holds 7 slices at p*256 (minUniformBufferOffsetAlignment). Slice p = {numTiles, PASS_TABLE[p].word, PASS_TABLE[p].shift, 100000}, where PASS_TABLE = [(0,0),(0,8),(0,16),(1,0),(1,8),(1,16),(1,24)] and word 0 = id, word 1 = z. PASS_TABLE is a TS constant shared by the pass and the CPU model. prepare() fills all 7 slices in one ArrayBuffer and issues exactly ONE queue.writeBuffer per frame; only numTiles changes. Nothing is rewritten between dispatches, so the writeBuffer-before-next-submit trap cannot occur. Bind group p is created once in setup(). It binds slice p ({buffer, offset: p*256, size: 16}, with layout minBindingSize 16) together with that pass's ping-pong direction (src = side p%2, dst = side (p+1)%2) and tsort-hist. So count, scan and scatter of pass p need only setBindGroup(0, bg[p]). There are no dynamic offsets and no override-specialised pipelines: 4 pipelines in total over 2 bind group layouts (the gather layout with 7 storage entries + 1 uniform, the sort layout with 5 storage + 1 uniform). The gather's bind group binds slice 0 and reads only numTiles and regionSize.
runnersUp.countHandling: The CPU works with an upper bound N = min(frame.transparentCount, MAX_ENTITIES = 100000). If N == 0, execute() encodes nothing and profileStages() returns []. prepare() has still reset transparent-draw-args to {6,0,0,0,0}, so the uber draw draws 0 instances and stale args from an earlier frame can never replay. Otherwise numTiles = ceil(N/1024) and N_pad = numTiles*1024, and every dispatch size derives from numTiles: gather numTiles*4, count numTiles, scan 1, scatter numTiles. The actual count n exists only on the GPU. Every gather thread computes it as the sum of min(instanceCount[14+k], 100000) for k = 0..11, then clamps it: n_eff = min(n, N_pad). The clamp is a safety net against a desync; with a correct transparentCount, n <= N <= N_pad. Elements [0, n_eff) are real and [n_eff, N_pad) are max-key sentinels, so the sort always sorts exactly N_pad elements in full tiles. That is why count and scatter need no bounds checks and no early returns, and why every barrier sits in uniform control flow. n_eff reaches only drawArgs.instanceCount, written by gather thread 0. There is no GPU->CPU readback and no dispatchWorkgroupsIndirect. Tiny counts: N = 1 is 1 tile, 1023 sentinels and the same 22 dispatches of 1-4 workgroups, a fixed floor of roughly 50-100 µs of dispatch/barrier latency.
