Many off-screen transparents: the cost follows transparentCount, not the visible count, bounded by the same 100k worst case.
runnersUp.bandwidthEstimate100k: N_pad = 100,352 (98 tiles), n ≈ 100,000. GATHER: reads visible-indices 4 B*n = 0.40 MB, bounds 16 B*n = 1.60 MB (cull fills each region in roughly ascending slot blocks; worst case fully random at 64 B/line = 6.4 MB), ids 4 B*n = 0.40 MB (worst 6.4 MB); writes keys+vals 12 B*N_pad = 1.20 MB. About 3.6 MB (14.4 MB worst). PER RADIX PASS: count reads keys 8 B*N = 0.80 MB and writes hist 0.10 MB; scan reads and writes hist 0.20 MB (L2-resident); scatter reads keys+vals 1.20 MB plus hist 0.10 MB and writes keys+vals 1.20 MB. About 3.6 MB logical per pass. The 780M's 2 MB L2 keeps the hist and most of the keys count just read, so DRAM traffic is about 2.1 MB per pass. 7 passes: about 25 MB logical, about 15 MB DRAM. FRAME TOTAL: about 29 MB logical, about 19 MB DRAM, up to about 40 MB with a random-order gather. At 60-100 GB/s: 0.19-0.48 ms typical, 0.67 ms worst (40 MB at 60 GB/s). FIXED COSTS: 22 dependent dispatches at about 3 µs of barrier/drain each ≈ 0.07 ms. The single-workgroup scan walk is 98 dependent L2 loads of about 130 ns ≈ 13 µs per pass, 0.09 ms per frame. Count/scatter tile latency: 98 workgroups ≈ 2 occupancy waves of about 48 resident 256-thread groups (12 CUs * 4), 13 barriers per scatter tile, about 15 µs per pass, 0.1 ms. COMPUTE: about 40 lane-ops per element per pass * 100k * 7 = 28M lane-ops against about 2 T lane-ops/s = 0.015 ms, not a factor. ESTIMATE: 0.45-0.75 ms at 100k, worst plausible about 0.9 ms. That is under the 1 ms target, but bandwidth-bound with a moderate margin. The profiler reports gather/count/scan/scatter separately, so any excess is visible per stage.
runnersUp.cpuReference: File ts/src/render/passes/transparent-sort-reference.ts. It is the single TS source of the constants: WG = 256, ROUNDS = 4, TILE = 1024, RADIX = 256, MASK_WORDS = 8, PASS_TABLE (7 x {word, shift}), FIRST_TRANSPARENT_ARG = 14, GATHER_REGIONS = 12. TransparentSortPass imports them for dispatch sizes and uniform slices. The file exports one function per kernel, with the same buffers as typed arrays of the same size: gatherCPU(args, visible, boundsBits: Uint32Array /* same bits as the upload */, ids, numTiles, regionSize), countCPU(keys, pass, numTiles, hist), scanCPU(hist, numTiles), scatterCPU(srcK, srcV, dstK, dstV, hist, pass, numTiles), and transparentSortCPU(), which runs gather + 7 x (count, scan, scatter) with the same ping-pong sides as the GPU. RULE: every barrier-separated WGSL phase is one `for (let lane = 0; lane < 256; lane++)` loop in TS. Workgroup memory is modelled with the same shapes: localHist Uint32Array(256), scanTmp Uint32Array(256), masks Uint32Array(2048), cursor Uint32Array(256). Atomics become plain |= and += (they commute, so the lane order in the model does not matter). The Hillis-Steele scan is modelled as its 8 read-loop then write-loop steps, not as a sequential prefix. Rank is the same popcount-of-lower-bits formula through a shared popcount32(). The z key is zSortKey(bits): -0 to +0, then the existing floatToSortKey mapping. Tests: (1) the model's vals[0..n) and drawCount equal an ORACLE, gathered elements sorted by Array.prototype.sort (stable since ES2019) on (zSortKey, id), for random z, all-equal z, negative/positive, -0/+0, ids up to MAX_EXTERNAL_ID, n in {1, 255, 256, 1023, 1024, 1025, 100000}, empty regions, non-empty Light2D regions 26/27 (must be excluded), and instanceCount sums above N_pad (clamp). (2) Shuffling the order inside every region gives an identical output (the frame-to-frame stability claim). (3) After each pass the order equals a stable sort by the digits so far (LSD invariant). (4) Text tests pin the WGSL consts to the TS ones (TILE, ROUNDS, 256, 14, 12, 0xFF) and check each file's storage-buffer budget (7 and 5, <= 8), minBindingSize and the 256-byte slice offsets; uniform-layout.test.ts covers SortParams automatically. (5) GPU check, not headless: a dev readback (in the style of debug-probe) of visible-indices regions 14..25, their instanceCounts, transparent-order and transparent-draw-args. The oracle over the read-back set must equal transparent-order[0..n) exactly, because keys are unique and the result is independent of cull's order. That is the only check that the WGSL transcribes the model.
risks: Bandwidth-bound on shared DRAM. The estimate is 0.45-0.75 ms at 100k with a moderate margin. Measured follow-ups if the profiler shows over 1 ms, simplest first: (a) skip the id passes above the CPU-known id high-water mark, e.g. no pass 2 below 2^16 ids, with the final pass always writing a fixed output buffer so parity does not move; (b) SoA keys so the 4 z passes stop carrying the id (about 13% of the traffic); (c) a 4-way unrolled scan walk or a larger TILE.
Fixed floor: 22 dependent dispatches cost roughly 50-100 µs even for 1 transparent entity. A single-workgroup fast path for N <= 1024 would be a second algorithm, so it is left out on purpose.

The cost follows transparentCount, the CPU bound, not the visible count: 100k transparent entities with 1k on screen still sort 100,352 elements. That stays within the target, but it is waste. The upgrade path, the gather writing dispatchWorkgroupsIndirect args and numTiles read from storage, is deliberately not taken.

transparentCount must be a true upper bound on the renderMeta bit-8 entities the GPU sees in the SAME frame, in every mode (Mode A render worker included, plumbed through GPURenderState). A low value makes the gather clamp at N_pad and silently drops entities from the transparent draw. Only the GPU readback check can see it.

A stale entity-ids buffer gives wrong tie-breaks at equal z and breaks cross-frame stability. Every slot remap, including swap-remove in flush_pending_despawns, assign_slot and snapshot restore, must flag the upload.

-0.0 normalisation and key building must stay integer-only (bounds bound as array<vec4u>). 'z + 0.0' or reading through f32 can be folded or flushed by the driver, because Vulkan does not guarantee signed-zero or denormal preservation, and CPU and GPU keys would then disagree.
The single-workgroup scan walk is about 13 µs per pass (98 dependent L2 loads) and grows linearly with the tile count. Visible as 'transparent-sort/scan'.

Storage budget: the gather sits at 7 of 8 entries. Adding one binding (a debug counter, a second key array) reaches the limit, and exceeding it returns an invalid pipeline without throwing. The budget test must cover both files and both layouts.

Correctness hinges on 'no early return before a barrier', which padding makes true. A future 'if (i >= n) { return; }' in count/scatter would be rejected by Tint's uniformity analysis, or, if written around the barrier, would break full-tile ranking. The CPU model's full-tile assumption mirrors this.

WGSL cannot run headless. The CPU model proves the algorithm; only the in-browser readback against the oracle proves the transcription. Unique keys make that comparison exact and independent of cull's nondeterministic order.

The profiler gets 22 markers per sorted frame (gather + 7 x count/scan/scatter, summed per name). The 256-marker budget is shared with light-groups (3 per SDF set). execute() uses one compute pass per stage so marks can sit between them.
NaN z sorts by bit pattern: negative NaNs first, positive NaNs last. Rust rejects non-finite input, so it is not expected, but it is not an error on the GPU.

The two new WGSL files need shaderSlots entries (probe = a throwaway TransparentSortPass) to be hot-reloadable. The old RadixSortPass, radix-sort.wgsl's unstable atomic scatter, cpuRadixSort and makeTransparentSortKey are deleted; only the floatToSortKey mapping survives, inside zSortKey.

issues.title: WRITE_KEYS override gates every scatter pass, not just the last, and production runs a variant no check ever exercises
issues.detail: The design has ONE scatter pipeline shared by all 7 passes: bind group p selects the pass, and the design says "No pipeline overrides are needed". Override constants are per pipeline. So the graft "the final pass writes only slots … selected by an override constant (WRITE_KEYS)" cannot limit itself to pass 6. The literal implementation is `if (WRITE_KEYS) { keysOut[dst] = key }` with WRITE_KEYS=false in production. It stops passes 0..5 from writing keys too, so pass 1 reads stale or uninitialised B keys and the order is garbage. Every verification in the plan runs the dev configuration (WRITE_KEYS=true): the CPU model mirrors the dev WGSL, readTransparentSort and the per-frame ring are dev-only, and "Keep keys-b for the per-stage readback in dev". So the only build users ever run is the only one never compared against the oracle. Concrete case: production, n = 2, z equal, ids {5, 3} gathered in the order [5, 3]. Pass 0 writes vals B = [3, 5] but no keys. Pass 1 reads keys B (zeros or last frame's), so its digits are wrong and it can reorder the vals arbitrarily.
issues.fix: Make pass 6 skip its key writes in every build, so dev and production run the same code. Either gate it as `if (params.passIndex != LAST_PASS) { keysOut[dst] = key }` (passIndex is already in the uniform), or give pass 6 its own scatter pipeline. The readback then derives the final keys on the CPU from order[], the captured bounds and the captured ids. If a dev/prod split is kept anyway, run the headless oracle tests on the CPU model in BOTH configurations, and add a mock-device test that the production pipeline set is the one the model covers.

issues.title: The "skip the id-high pass" graft is wrong with the chosen key packing, and skipping any pass breaks the baked A/B bind groups
issues.detail: The key is lo = (zKey << 20) | id and hi = zKey >> 12. Pass 2's digit is lo bits 16..23, which is id bits 16..19 PLUS zKey bits 0..3. No pass is purely "id-high". Suppose the id high-water mark is < 2^16 and pass 2 is skipped. Take a at z = 1.0 (bits 0x3F800000, zKey 0xBF800000) with id 5, and b at z = nextafter(1.0) (0x3F800001, zKey 0xBF800001) with id 3. Passes 0-1 order them by id: b, a. Passes 3-6 see equal digits (zKey bits 4..31 are identical) and stay stable. The result is b, a. The 52-bit key order is a, b, because zKey_a < zKey_b. Separately, bind group p bakes the direction (even A→B, odd B→A). If pass 2 is skipped, pass 1's output sits in A while pass 3's bind group reads B. "A fixed output buffer so the parity never moves" does not fix the middle passes.
issues.fix: Repack the key as hi = zKey (the whole word) and lo = id (20 bits). That is still 7 passes (lo: 8, 8 and 4 bits; hi: 4 × 8), with digit(k, p) = p < 3 ? (lo >> 8p) & 0xFF : (hi >> 8(p-3)) & 0xFF. Pass 2 is then purely id bits 16..19 and can be skipped when the id high-water mark is < 2^16, and the z digits become byte-aligned for the trivial-digit skip. Any pass skipping needs bind groups for both directions (14, indexed by (pass, parity)), chosen on the CPU from the number of passes actually run. The last pass run must write transparent-order, and a CPU-model test must pin the skipped configurations against the oracle.

issues.title: Fused upsweep (atomicAdd into tiles from scatter p) races with scatter p's own reads of the single shared tile table
issues.detail: The design keeps ONE tile table, `hist.tiles`, "reused by every pass". Scatter p reads it in phase 0 (`cursor[j] = digitBase[p*256+j] + tiles[t*256+j]`, the scanned offsets for pass p). The proposed first optimisation has the same scatter dispatch atomicAdd into `tiles[dst/1024][digit_{p+1}]`. Workgroups of one dispatch have no ordering. If workgroup B scatters and increments row t_A for pass p+1 before workgroup A runs phase 0, A reads prefix + extra counts. Its dst values then shift, which either collides with other writes or trips `dst >= n`. The rows also need zeroing before the accumulation, and `tiles` would have to become array<atomic<u32>>. "Commutative, so still deterministic" is true of the counts but beside the point. Also, the CPU model's race checker covers workgroup memory only. It runs whole workgroups sequentially, so it cannot flag a cross-workgroup global read-after-write inside one dispatch. It would catch this only as an oracle mismatch under some shuffles.
issues.fix: If the fusion is ever done, double-buffer the tile table: tilesRead for pass p, tilesAccum (atomic) for p+1, cleared with encoder.clearBuffer before each scatter dispatch. Swap the roles per pass through the per-pass bind groups (hist grows by 98×256 u32, and the binding count is unchanged if both live in sort-hist at fixed offsets). Add a per-dispatch global-memory conflict checker to the CPU model: an address written, atomically or not, by one workgroup and read non-atomically by another in the same dispatch must throw.

issues.title: Per-digit min/max graft does not fit the 7 reserved header words and races with the gather's non-atomic header write
issues.detail: Recording a max of d and a max of MASK^d for each of 7 passes needs 14 words. The 64-B SortState has only words 9-15, which is 7 words. Packing two values into one word defeats atomicMax. The header is written non-atomically by workgroup 0, lane 0, while every other workgroup of the same dispatch would atomicMax those words. If that write covers the reserved words (for example a whole-struct assignment `state = SortState(...)`), a plain store of 0 can land after other workgroups' atomicMax and lose their maxima. The result is a nondeterministic "trivial pass" report, which is exactly what a later skip decision would trust.
issues.fix: Put the 14 atomic maxima in hist.diag[1..14]: diag has 16 atomic words, is already zeroed in prepare(), and is already in the dev ring's 64-B copy. Keep the lane-0 header write to words 0..8 only, and pin that in a text test.

issues.title: The CPU bound is the only source of truth for coverage: a zero or undefined transparentCount drops every transparent entity, even in dev
issues.detail: At L == 0 the design dispatches nothing and ForwardPass skips the uber draw. The overflow flag and the dev ring are computed by the gather, which does not run, so a wrong bound of 0 is silent in dev as well: 'checked every frame in dev' does not hold for the most likely failure. That failure is a bridge (Mode A, per the risks) that does not carry the field. If the field is undefined rather than 0, L = Math.min(undefined, 100000) = NaN. `NaN === 0` is false, so execute() calls dispatchWorkgroups(Math.ceil(NaN/256)). GPUSize32 is [EnforceRange], so it throws a TypeError inside render(), which per CLAUDE.md stops the engine for good. Yet a true bound is always available: cull puts every idx < entityCount in at most one bucket, so raw <= entityCount.
issues.fix: Bound the gather dispatch and GatherParams.limit by min(entityCount, MAX_ENTITIES), which is always a true bound. Have the gather write {numTiles, 1, 1} into transparent-args (for example words 9-11, a 4-byte-aligned offset of 36; the buffer already has INDIRECT) and use dispatchWorkgroupsIndirect for upsweep and scatter. Their size then follows n, not the CPU bound. Keep transparentCount only as the zero-skip, normalise it with `?? entityCount`, and in dev assert it on the CPU against the count of renderMeta bit 8 with type < 6 in state.renderMeta (the full array is on the CPU in every mode).

issues.title: 'Capacity cannot be exceeded by construction' relies on entityCount <= 100000, which nothing enforces
issues.detail: types.ts accepts any maxEntities, and RawAPI.spawn is not counted: hyperion.ts:426 checks only handle spawns. With entityCount > 100000 the renderer's full-upload writeBuffer exceeds the fixed buffers and is dropped. CullPass still dispatches totalEntities = entityCount, so it emits idx >= 100000, and a bucket with more than 100000 entries spills past its region (region 25 spills into the Light2D region 26). The gather stays inside its regions, since i < n <= 100000 gives j < 100000. But the slot VALUES it gathers can be >= MAX_ENTITIES, so bounds[slot] and entityIds[slot] are out-of-bounds reads (robust-access clamped). Several slots then read the same clamped id, giving duplicate keys and an order that changes between frames, and the uber vertex shader reads transforms[slot] out of range. The sort's own buffers stay safe thanks to the MAX clamp on L, but the claim that the only reachable over-count is a wrong CPU bound is false.
issues.fix: Enforce the cap at the source: reject maxEntities > MAX_ENTITIES in resolveConfig, count RawAPI spawns against the limit, or clamp entityCount to MAX_ENTITIES in renderer.render with a one-time warning. Also add a GPU guard in the gather: if slot >= regionSize, drop the entry and atomicOr a diag bit. Then say in the design which of these makes the sort's input well-formed.

issues.title: The dev readback copies inputs from three buffers that have no COPY_SRC usage
issues.detail: engine.debug.readTransparentSort() copies the gather's inputs: indirect-args, visible-indices regions 14..25 and entity-bounds (plus entity-ids). The design adds dev COPY_SRC only to its own buffers and to entity-ids. In the repo, 'entity-bounds' is STORAGE|COPY_DST (renderer.ts:233-236), 'visible-indices' is STORAGE only (238-241) and 'indirect-args' is STORAGE|INDIRECT|COPY_DST (243-246). Only entity-transforms gets the dev COPY_SRC (229). A copyBufferToBuffer from any of the three is a validation error that invalidates the encoder. RenderGraph.render records the whole frame in one encoder and one submit (render-graph.ts). So the readback drops the entire frame, swapchain included, and returns no data. The CPU model then has nothing to replay, and the headline check (the model reproduces every stage bit for bit from the frame's exact inputs) cannot run on the GPU at all.
issues.fix: In renderer.ts add `(dev ? GPUBufferUsage.COPY_SRC : 0)` to entity-bounds, visible-indices and indirect-args, the same way entity-transforms has it. Add a test that builds the renderer's buffer descriptors with __DEV__ true and asserts COPY_SRC on every buffer the readback copies from. Also wrap the readback submit in validation and out-of-memory error scopes, as DebugProbe does, so a missing usage rejects the promise instead of answering zeros.

issues.title: If ForwardPass does not read the sort outputs, the sort pass is culled or ordered by accident
issues.detail: The design never says that ForwardPass must list 'transparent-order' and 'transparent-args' in its reads. It also never says whether TransparentSortPass is optional. RenderGraph.compile seeds the alive set only with non-optional passes and swapchain writers, then follows reads backwards. The pass it replaces is the precedent: RadixSortPass is `optional = true` and writes 'transparent-vals-sorted' (radix-sort-pass.ts:17-20), ForwardPass reads only ['visible-indices','entity-transforms','tex-indices','indirect-args','render-meta','prim-params'] (forward-pass.ts:41), so the old pass was culled every frame. That is one reason it 'never ran'. Repeating the pattern gives this: prepare() still resets transparent-args to {6,0,0,0,0}, the sort is never encoded, and the uber draw issues 0 instances. Every transparent entity disappears with no error. If the pass is instead made non-optional without that read, it runs only because Kahn's queue happens to dequeue it before ForwardPass (both depend only on cull, and it is registered first in the scene factory at renderer.ts:466). Registering LightGroupsPass or an overlay in a different order could then run the uber draw before the gather, on the previous frame's order buffer.
issues.fix: Make ForwardPass (lit and unlit) declare `reads` of 'transparent-order' and 'transparent-args', and keep TransparentSortPass optional so graph liveness follows from that read. Add a compose test in graph-assembly: for each of the 3 composites with lighting on and off, 'transparent-sort' must be in compile() output after 'cull' and before 'forward'.

issues.title: transparentCount is not carried in Mode B, and a missing value makes dispatchWorkgroups throw inside render()
issues.detail: The design names only Mode A as needing to carry transparentCount. But every bridge rebuilds the render state field by field: engine-worker.ts:191-205 builds the Mode B/A message, the Mode B bridge copies it at worker-bridge.ts:131-151, Mode A at 262-285, and Mode C at 496-513. A new field is dropped unless all four sites add it, and Mode B is the harness default. Two outcomes follow. With the repo's usual `rs.x ?? 0` default, L = 0 and no transparent entity is drawn in Mode B. Without a default, L = min(undefined, 100000) = NaN, so `Math.ceil(NaN/256)` goes to dispatchWorkgroups. Its argument is GPUSize32 = [EnforceRange] unsigned long, so it throws a TypeError. That throw happens inside renderer.render inside tickFn, which GameLoop does not isolate, so requestAnimationFrame is never re-armed and the engine stops for good (CLAUDE.md, RenderGraph bullet).
issues.fix: Add transparentCount at all four sites plus GPURenderState/FrameState, and test each bridge's state for it. In the pass, compute `const bound = Number.isFinite(frame.transparentCount) ? frame.transparentCount >>> 0 : frame.entityCount; L = Math.min(bound, MAX_ENTITIES)`. entityCount is always a valid upper bound, so a missing field costs time, never entities or a throw. Use the same L in prepare, profileStages and execute.

issues.title: Derivatives inside the uber shader's per-instance type switch fail WGSL derivative uniformity
issues.detail: The consumer of this pass is one uber pipeline over types 0..5. Its fragment stage has to branch on the primitive type, which is read from renderMeta through a fragment input (the flat entityIdx), so the branch is non-uniform under WGSL uniformity analysis. Three bodies it would inline take derivatives: line.wgsl:192 `fwidth(in.uv.y)`, bezier.wgsl:170 `fwidth(d)`, and msdf-text.wgsl:148-149 `dpdx/dpdy`. The repo already records the rule at line.wgsl:187-189: 'Derivatives need uniform control flow: first, before any branch'. derivative_uniformity is an error by default. The uber module then fails to compile, so the graph that contains it is rejected by RenderGraphHost, or, for the synchronously built initial graph, only logged, which leaves every ForwardPass draw invalid (black canvas). No headless test can see this.
issues.fix: Either add `diagnostic(off, derivative_uniformity)` on the uber fs entry or on the switch, with a comment giving the reason: the type is flat per instance and a 2x2 quad never spans two triangles, so the branch is quad-uniform. Or hoist every derivative before the switch: fwidth(uv.y), dpdx/dpdy(uv), and fwidth of the bezier distance, which means computing sdBezier unconditionally. Validate with getCompilationInfo on the AMD adapter before building the rest, and add a text test that no derivative call sits inside the type switch unless the diagnostic is present.

issues.title: The 3-deep dev MAP_READ ring copied every frame has no skip rule, so a busy ring invalidates whole frames
issues.detail: The design copies transparent-args (64 B) and diag (64 B) into a 3-deep MAP_READ ring 'after the pass every frame'. queue.submit requires every buffer the command buffer references to be unmapped. A ring buffer with a pending mapAsync is not, so the submit fails validation and the whole frame is dropped (one encoder, one submit). mapAsync resolves only after the GPU finishes that frame and the event loop runs the callback. At the 100k target on the iGPU, where the GPU is the bottleneck, or with a busy main thread in Mode B/C, all three slots can be pending at once. That drops frames, in dev only and exactly during the profiling runs this phase depends on. GpuProfiler already solves the same problem: beginFrame returns false 'when every readback buffer is still in flight' and records nothing.
issues.fix: Take a ring slot only when its state is 'unmapped' (track it: set pending before mapAsync, clear it after unmap). Otherwise skip the copy for that frame and count the skips. Add a mock-device test in which all three slots stay pending: execute() must encode no copy into them.

issues.title: The final-only sort-hist readback cannot pinpoint whether upsweep or scan diverged
issues.detail: Upsweep writes the per-tile histograms into hist.tiles. Scan then overwrites them in place with column prefixes, and the next pass's upsweep overwrites the table again. The design reads sort-hist only at the end ('final keys-b/order, sort-hist, transparent-args'), plus keys/vals after each pass. What is left for checking is digitBase for all 7 passes and pass 6's scanned table. No upsweep output and none of the tables from passes 0-5 can be observed. So the claim that 'the per-stage readback... pinpoints the first kernel that diverges' holds for gather and scatter, but not for upsweep or scan.
issues.fix: With {stages:true}, copy sort-hist, or only the first ceil(n/1024)*256 tile words plus digitBase, after each upsweep and after each scan: 14 copies of at most 107 KB. The compute pass is already ended after every dispatch (22 compute passes). Compare them with cpuUpsweep and cpuScan outputs word for word.

issues.title: The listed follow-up optimisations hide WebGPU hazards: a shared tile table, atomics in read-only state, indirect args and the 8-binding limit
issues.detail: (a) 'Fuse upsweep p+1 into scatter p through global atomicAdd on tiles[dst/1024][digit_{p+1}]' writes to the ONLY tile table while other workgroups of the same scatter dispatch still read their pass-p prefixes from it in phase 0. Workgroups have no ordering between them, so offsets get corrupted. The table would also need zeroing, and it is a plain array<u32>, not atomic. (b) Trivial-digit detection by 'atomicMax ... in gather and upsweep' into the state header cannot work in the sort module. Atomics are only allowed in read_write storage or workgroup memory. Making `state` read_write there would make `n` non-uniform, and the early-return guard before barriers then fails to compile. The later indirect dispatch that skips passes cannot take its args from sort-hist either: that buffer is bound as writable storage in the same dispatch, and INDIRECT plus writable storage in one dispatch's usage scope is a validation error. (c) Fusing pass 0 into the gather still needs a global prefix between the histogram half and the scatter half, so it cannot be one dispatch. The scatter half binds drawArgs, visibleIndices, bounds, entityIds, state, hist, keysOut and valsOut: exactly 8 storage bindings. Any extra binding, such as a separate diag buffer or keeping sort-keys-a for the readback, makes the pipeline invalid.
issues.fix: Record these constraints next to the follow-ups. (a) Keep two fixed-size tile tables inside SortHist (capacity is fixed), declare the accumulating one as array<atomic<u32>>, zero it in scan p, and read the other one. (b) Put the min/max atomics in sort-hist, keep state as var<storage, read> in transparent-sort.wgsl with its own atomic-free struct declaration, and have indirect-dispatch args written only by the gather into a buffer the sort dispatches bind read-only, such as an extended transparent-args. (c) Add the fused gather to the text test that counts storage bindings per layout, with a hard <= 8 assertion.

issues.title: No radix pass is id-only, so skipping the 'id-high' pass by an id high-water mark mis-sorts
issues.detail: The key is lo = (zKey << 20) | id and hi = zKey >> 12. Pass 2's 8-bit digit is bits 16-23, which are id bits 16-19 AND zKey bits 0-3. The suggested cheap step, 'skip the id-high pass using a CPU-known id high-water mark', drops pass 2 whenever every id is below 65536. Two entities whose z differs only in the low 4 mantissa bits, which is common for arbitrary floats, are then ordered only by the higher z digits and by the id digits. Their relative order becomes the input order, which is nondeterministic from cull. That breaks both the back-to-front rule and frame-to-frame stability, and nothing in diag detects it.
issues.fix: Widen the id field to 24 bits: key = (zKey << 24) | id (56 bits, still 7 passes of 8), with lo = (zKey << 24) | id and hi = zKey >> 8. Passes 0-2 are then id-only and passes 3-6 z-only, so both 'skip the id-high pass' and 'skip the 4 z passes when z is constant' become byte-exact. Update the digit() helper, the CPU model and the text-agreement test together.
